```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
librarian::shelf(
  calcofi4r, cmocean, DBI, dplyr, DT, duckdb, ggplot2, ggrepel, glue, gsw, here, htmltools, knitr,
  patchwork, purrr, readr, rnaturalearth, sf, stringr, terra, tibble, tidyr,
  quiet = T)
options(readr.show_col_types = F, knitr.kable.NA = "")

# constants ----
VER       <- "v2026.11.09"    # the release this page is pinned to (latest.txt on 2026-11-13)
CRUISE    <- "2026-11-33P4"   # R/V Sally Ride, 31 October to 7 November 2026
core      <- c("093.3 028.0", "093.3 030.0")   # the two stations at the heart of the warm layer
BASE_URL  <- "https://storage.googleapis.com/calcofi-db"
DIR_DATA  <- here("data/2026-11_temperature-anomaly")   # small tables this page writes or keeps
DIR_CACHE <- Sys.getenv("CALCOFI_CACHE_DIR", tools::R_user_dir("calcofi", "cache"))
KM_PER_STATION <- 7.386       # +proj=calcofi: a line is equidistant, 7.386 km (4 nmi) per station unit
ANOM_MAX  <- 13               # the top of the departure scale, shared by the map and the section (°C)
dir.create(DIR_DATA, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)

# brand v2 inks (https://calcofi.io/brand/v2/theme.css) ----
INK      <- "#182b49"
MUTED    <- "#66686a"
GRID     <- "#e4e4e4"
SAND     <- "#f5f0e6"
STONE    <- "#b6b1a9"
COL_2026 <- "#b3261e"
COL_2015 <- "#c69214"
COL_NORM <- "#00629b"

# number formats: one decimal, a signed departure with a true minus, thousands ----
f1  <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
fs  <- function(x, d = 1) sub("-", "−", sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f"), x), fixed = T)
fk  <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = T)
fsa <- function(x, d = 0) ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 * 10^-d, formatC(0, format = "f", digits = d), fs(x, d))   # axis labels: a bare 0
nb  <- function(x) gsub("–", "\u2060–\u2060", gsub("-", "\u2011", x, fixed = T), fixed = T)   # no line break inside a key or a range
dt_ <- function(d, ...) datatable(
  d, rownames = F, class = "compact stripe", extensions = "Buttons",
  options = list(dom = "Bfrtip", pageLength = 12, buttons = c("copy", "csv")), ...)

# plot theme ----
theme_story <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text                  = element_text(colour = INK),
      axis.text             = element_text(colour = MUTED),
      panel.grid.major      = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor      = element_blank(),
      plot.title            = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.12)),
      plot.subtitle         = element_text(colour = MUTED, size = rel(0.9), margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption          = element_text(colour = MUTED, size = rel(0.72), hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.15),
      plot.title.position   = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      strip.text            = element_text(face = "bold", colour = INK, hjust = 0),
      legend.position       = "none")}
```

```{r}
#| label: release
#| include: false
# the release catalog is the only source of object URLs (calcofi4r::cc_catalog() / cc_release_sources()):
# every table below is read from the URLs the catalog lists, never from a path built by hand
CAT   <- cc_catalog(VER)
con   <- dbConnect(duckdb())
d_src <- tibble()   # every object this page reads: the table under "Data sources"

# a release object by its catalog URL, kept in a local cache (objects are content-addressed and immutable) ----
mirror <- function(url) {
  path <- file.path(DIR_CACHE, sub(paste0(BASE_URL, "/"), "", url, fixed = T))
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = T, showWarnings = F)
    curl::curl_download(url, paste0(path, ".part"), quiet = T)
    file.rename(paste0(path, ".part"), path)}
  path}

# a DuckDB view over one release table: all of its objects, or the partitions named in `parts` ----
release_view <- function(table, parts = NULL, cols = "*", name = table) {
  src  <- cc_release_sources(CAT, table)
  urls <- src$urls
  if (!is.null(parts))
    urls <- unique(unlist(lapply(parts, \(p) grep(glue("={p}/"), urls, fixed = T, value = T))))   # the catalog lists some objects twice
  stopifnot(length(urls) >= 1, is.null(parts) || length(urls) == length(parts))
  files <- vapply(urls, mirror, "", USE.NAMES = F)
  dbExecute(con, glue(
    "CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {name} AS SELECT {cols} FROM read_parquet(",
    "[{paste0(\"'\", files, \"'\", collapse = ', ')}], hive_partitioning = {tolower(src$hive)}, union_by_name = true)"))
  d_src <<- bind_rows(d_src, tibble(
    table = table, partition = if (is.null(parts)) NA_character_ else parts, url = urls, mb = file.size(files) / 1e6))
  invisible(urls)}

# the tables this page reads ----
release_view("cruise")
release_view("sample", cols = "* EXCLUDE (geom)")
release_view("sample_measurement")
release_view("measurement_type")
release_view("obs_env",      parts = c("temperature_ave", "temperature", "salinity_ave_corr", "salinity"))
release_view("climatology",  parts = c("temperature_ave", "temperature", "salinity_ave_corr", "salinity", "mld_sigma_theta_0125"))
release_view("obs_ctd_full", parts = CRUISE)
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-cell
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cell AS
-- every temperature cell in the record with its departure from the release's own climatology.
-- a CELL is one cruise x station (site_key) x 10 m depth bin of one dataset: the mean of its quality-ok observations.
-- its baseline is the climatology row of the SAME dataset, station, depth bin and measurement type for the CRUISE's
-- month (obs_env.cruise_month = cruise.month_median), the rule every CalCOFI app applies. A cell whose month has no
-- monthly baseline keeps anom NULL: never 0. The seasonal baseline (the cruise's season) rides along as anom_season.
WITH o AS (
  SELECT dataset_key, measurement_type, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin,
         any_value(cruise_month) AS cruise_month, any_value(year) AS cruise_year,
         avg(value) AS v, count(*) AS n_obs, avg(depth_min_m) AS depth_m,
         avg(latitude) AS latitude, avg(longitude) AS longitude, min(datetime) AS datetime
  FROM obs_env
  WHERE measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'temperature')          -- CTD sensor-pair average; bottle (QC'd)
    AND dataset_key IN ('calcofi_ctd-cast', 'calcofi_bottle')
    AND qual_ok AND value IS NOT NULL AND depth_bin IS NOT NULL AND site_key IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ALL)
SELECT o.*,
       TRY_CAST(split_part(o.site_key, ' ', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS line,
       TRY_CAST(split_part(o.site_key, ' ', 2) AS DOUBLE) AS station,
       c.clim_mean, c.clim_sd, c.clim_n, c.n_cruises, c.season_mean, c.season_sd, c.season_n_cruises,
       o.v - c.clim_mean   AS anom,
       o.v - c.season_mean AS anom_season
FROM o
LEFT JOIN climatology c
  ON c.dataset_key = o.dataset_key AND c.measurement_type = o.measurement_type AND c.site_key = o.site_key
 AND c.month = o.cruise_month AND c.depth_bin = o.depth_bin
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-cruise-ref
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cruise_ref AS
-- one row per cruise: its dates, its month (the median cast month) and the stage of its CTD casts
SELECT c.cruise_key, c.year, c.month_median AS cruise_month, c.date_min, c.date_max, c.date_median, c.ship_name,
       (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT s.data_stage, ', ' ORDER BY s.data_stage) FROM sample s
        WHERE s.cruise_key = c.cruise_key AND s.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND s.sample_type = 'cast') AS ctd_stage
FROM cruise c
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-cast-1m
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cast_1m AS
-- the November 2026 casts at the CTD's full 1 m resolution (obs_ctd_full), with their station
SELECT s.site_key, f.sample_key, right(f.sample_key, 1) AS direction, f.depth_min_m AS depth_m,
       f.measurement_type, f.measurement_value AS value, f.measurement_qual, f.datetime, f.latitude, f.longitude
FROM obs_ctd_full f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
WHERE f.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'temperature_1', 'temperature_2', 'salinity_1', 'salinity_2',
                             'salinity_ave_corr', 'sigma_theta_1', 'salinity_btl', 'oxygen_btl_ml_l', 'oxygen_ml_l_1')
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-interp
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO interp_profile(col) AS TABLE
-- an anomaly (or temperature) profile on every 10 m bin from 0 to 190 m: linear interpolation IN DEPTH between the
-- bins that were sampled (never across more than 60 m, never beyond the deepest or above the shallowest sampled bin,
-- never in time or between stations). It puts the bottle series (standard depths) on the CTD's footing.
WITH a AS (SELECT dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin, col AS a FROM cell WHERE col IS NOT NULL AND depth_bin < 260),
casts AS (SELECT DISTINCT dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key FROM a),
t AS (SELECT c.*, b.depth_bin FROM casts c, (SELECT unnest(range(0, 200, 10)) AS depth_bin) b)
SELECT t.dataset_key, t.cruise_key, t.site_key, t.depth_bin,
       CASE WHEN lo.depth_bin = hi.depth_bin THEN lo.a
            WHEN hi.depth_bin - lo.depth_bin <= 60 THEN lo.a + (hi.a - lo.a) * (t.depth_bin - lo.depth_bin) / (hi.depth_bin - lo.depth_bin) END AS a
FROM t
ASOF LEFT JOIN a lo ON lo.dataset_key = t.dataset_key AND lo.cruise_key = t.cruise_key AND lo.site_key = t.site_key AND lo.depth_bin <= t.depth_bin
ASOF LEFT JOIN a hi ON hi.dataset_key = t.dataset_key AND hi.cruise_key = t.cruise_key AND hi.site_key = t.site_key AND hi.depth_bin >= t.depth_bin
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-prof
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE prof AS
-- the three interpolated profiles side by side. The key columns are the USING columns (coalesced over the three sides):
-- a cruise in a month with no monthly normal (September 1997) has no row on the anom side and must keep its keys.
SELECT dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin, m.a AS anom, s.a AS anom_season, v.a AS temp
FROM interp_profile(anom) m
FULL JOIN interp_profile(anom_season) s USING (dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin)
FULL JOIN interp_profile(v) v USING (dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin)
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-station-layer
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE station_layer AS
-- one row per cast x layer: the depth-mean where the layer is complete (every 10 m bin of it present)
WITH l AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('surface (0-10 m)', 0, 0), ('0-50 m', 0, 40), ('50-200 m', 50, 190), ('0-200 m', 0, 190)) AS t(layer, b0, b1))
SELECT p.dataset_key, p.cruise_key, p.site_key, l.layer,
       TRY_CAST(split_part(p.site_key, ' ', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS line, TRY_CAST(split_part(p.site_key, ' ', 2) AS DOUBLE) AS station,
       CASE WHEN count(p.anom)        = (l.b1 - l.b0) / 10 + 1 THEN avg(p.anom) END        AS anom,
       CASE WHEN count(p.anom_season) = (l.b1 - l.b0) / 10 + 1 THEN avg(p.anom_season) END AS anom_season,
       CASE WHEN count(p.temp)        = (l.b1 - l.b0) / 10 + 1 THEN avg(p.temp) END        AS temp
FROM prof p JOIN l ON p.depth_bin BETWEEN l.b0 AND l.b1
GROUP BY p.dataset_key, p.cruise_key, p.site_key, l.layer, l.b0, l.b1
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-cruise-layer
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cruise_layer AS
-- every cruise's layer mean over ONE fixed set of stations: the ones the November 2026 cruise occupied.
-- `covered`: the cruise occupied at least 60 % of the stations November 2026 has for that layer.
WITH fp AS (SELECT DISTINCT site_key FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = '2026-11-33P4' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast'),
n26 AS (SELECT layer, count(anom) AS n_ref, count(anom_season) AS n_ref_season FROM station_layer WHERE cruise_key = '2026-11-33P4' GROUP BY layer),
x AS (
  SELECT s.dataset_key, s.cruise_key, s.layer,
         count(s.anom) AS n_sta, avg(s.anom) AS anom, max(s.anom) AS anom_max_station,
         count(s.anom_season) AS n_sta_season, avg(s.anom_season) AS anom_season, avg(s.temp) AS temp
  FROM station_layer s SEMI JOIN fp USING (site_key)
  GROUP BY ALL)
SELECT x.*, n26.n_ref, n26.n_ref_season,
       x.n_sta >= 0.6 * n26.n_ref AS covered, x.n_sta_season >= 0.6 * n26.n_ref_season AS covered_season,
       c.year, c.cruise_month, c.date_min, c.date_max
FROM x JOIN n26 USING (layer) LEFT JOIN cruise_ref c USING (cruise_key)
```

```{sql}
--| label: sql-paired
--| connection: con
--| include: false
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE paired AS
-- the strictest comparison: November 2026 against every other cruise ON THE STATIONS THEY SHARE, by three yardsticks:
-- the departure from the monthly normal, from the seasonal normal, and the layer's temperature itself (no baseline)
WITH ref AS (SELECT site_key, layer, anom AS a26, anom_season AS s26, temp AS t26 FROM station_layer WHERE cruise_key = '2026-11-33P4' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast')
SELECT s.dataset_key, s.cruise_key, s.layer,
       count(*)           FILTER (WHERE s.anom IS NOT NULL AND r.a26 IS NOT NULL)        AS n_month,
       avg(s.anom)        FILTER (WHERE s.anom IS NOT NULL AND r.a26 IS NOT NULL)        AS anom_other,
       avg(r.a26)         FILTER (WHERE s.anom IS NOT NULL AND r.a26 IS NOT NULL)        AS anom_2026,
       count(*)           FILTER (WHERE s.anom_season IS NOT NULL AND r.s26 IS NOT NULL) AS n_season,
       avg(s.anom_season) FILTER (WHERE s.anom_season IS NOT NULL AND r.s26 IS NOT NULL) AS season_other,
       avg(r.s26)         FILTER (WHERE s.anom_season IS NOT NULL AND r.s26 IS NOT NULL) AS season_2026,
       count(*)           FILTER (WHERE s.temp IS NOT NULL AND r.t26 IS NOT NULL)        AS n_temp,
       avg(s.temp)        FILTER (WHERE s.temp IS NOT NULL AND r.t26 IS NOT NULL)        AS temp_other,
       avg(r.t26)         FILTER (WHERE s.temp IS NOT NULL AND r.t26 IS NOT NULL)        AS temp_2026
FROM station_layer s JOIN ref r USING (site_key, layer)
WHERE s.cruise_key <> '2026-11-33P4'
GROUP BY ALL
```

```{r}
#| label: key-numbers
#| include: false
q <- function(sql, ...) dbGetQuery(con, glue_sql(sql, ..., .con = con)) |> as_tibble()

# two casts hold bad values, not warm water (shown under "Single measurements"): left out where events are compared ----
invisible(dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW cell_ok AS
  SELECT * FROM cell
  WHERE NOT (cruise_key = '1994-01-31JD' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND site_key = '093.3 028.0' AND depth_bin >= 510)
    AND NOT (cruise_key = '1959-10-31OR' AND site_key = '093.3 035.0')"))

# the record cell and the previous record ----
d_cell26 <- q("SELECT * FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND anom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY anom DESC")
top      <- d_cell26[1, ]
prev     <- q("SELECT * FROM cell WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} AND anom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY anom DESC LIMIT 1")
d_share  <- q("
  WITH r AS (SELECT cruise_key, anom, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY anom DESC) AS rk FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL)
  SELECT count(*) AS n_cells, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n_cruises,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE rk <= 50  AND cruise_key = {CRUISE}) AS of_top_50,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE rk <= 100 AND cruise_key = {CRUISE}) AS of_top_100,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND anom > {prev$anom}) AS n_above_prev,
         min(substr(cruise_key, 1, 4)) AS yr0
  FROM r")
n_cruises_all <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n FROM cell")$n

# each earlier warm event's largest single departure, by the monthly normal and by the seasonal one ----
d_evmax <- q("
  WITH ev AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('1957–59', 1957, 1959), ('1982–83', 1982, 1983), ('1997–98', 1997, 1998), ('2014–16', 2014, 2016)) t(event, y0, y1))
  SELECT ev.event, max(c.anom) AS anom, arg_max(c.cruise_key, c.anom) AS cruise_key, arg_max(c.site_key, c.anom) AS site_key,
         arg_max(c.depth_bin, c.anom) AS depth_bin, max(c.anom_season) AS anom_s, arg_max(c.cruise_key, c.anom_season) AS cruise_s,
         arg_max(c.site_key, c.anom_season) AS site_s, arg_max(c.depth_bin, c.anom_season) AS bin_s
  FROM cell_ok c JOIN ev ON c.cruise_year BETWEEN ev.y0 AND ev.y1 GROUP BY ev.event ORDER BY ev.event")
evm <- function(e) d_evmax[d_evmax$event == e, ]
sta <- function(site_key) sub("^0", "", gsub(" 0+", " ", site_key))      # "093.3 030.0" -> "93.3 30.0"
stopifnot(abs(c(evm("1982–83")$anom, evm("1997–98")$anom, evm("1997–98")$anom_s) - 6) < 0.6)   # "near +6 °C" in the summary

# layer means over the stations the cruise occupied ----
d_layer <- q("SELECT * FROM cruise_layer WHERE covered") |>
  mutate(series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"))
lay <- function(layer_, cruise_ = CRUISE, ds = "calcofi_ctd-cast") d_layer |>
  filter(layer == layer_, cruise_key == cruise_, dataset_key == ds)
runner <- function(layer_) d_layer |> filter(layer == layer_, cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice_max(anom, n = 1, with_ties = F)

# the cruise, station by station ----
d_sta <- q("
  SELECT s.site_key, s.line, s.station, s.layer, s.anom, s.anom_season, s.temp, p.lat, p.lon, p.t0
  FROM station_layer s
  JOIN (SELECT site_key, avg(latitude) AS lat, avg(longitude) AS lon, min(datetime) AS t0 FROM cell
        WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND depth_bin = 0 GROUP BY site_key) p USING (site_key)
  WHERE s.cruise_key = {CRUISE}") |>
  mutate(km_offshore = (station - 26.4) * KM_PER_STATION)
sfc   <- d_sta |> filter(layer == "surface (0-10 m)", !is.na(anom))
# the inner Southern California Bight: the stations inshore of the front the cruise crossed
inner <- sfc |> filter((line >= 88 & station <= 37) | (line < 88 & station <= 51))
outer <- sfc |> anti_join(inner, by = "site_key")
stopifnot(min(inner$anom) > max(outer$anom))   # the two groups do not overlap: a front, not a gradient

# salinity and mixed-layer depth on the inshore end of line 93.3 ----
d_sal <- q("
  SELECT o.site_key, o.depth_bin, avg(o.value) AS sal, any_value(c.clim_mean) AS clim, any_value(c.clim_sd) AS sd
  FROM obs_env o LEFT JOIN climatology c
    ON c.measurement_type = o.measurement_type AND c.dataset_key = o.dataset_key AND c.site_key = o.site_key
   AND c.depth_bin = o.depth_bin AND c.month = o.cruise_month
  WHERE o.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND o.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND o.qual_ok
    AND o.site_key IN ({core*}) AND o.depth_bin <= 40
  GROUP BY ALL")
d_mld <- q("
  SELECT s.site_key, m.measurement_value AS mld, c.clim_mean AS clim, c.n_cruises
  FROM sample_measurement m JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  LEFT JOIN climatology c ON c.measurement_type = m.measurement_type AND c.site_key = s.site_key AND c.month = 11 AND c.depth_bin IS NULL
  WHERE s.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND m.measurement_type = 'mld_sigma_theta_0125'
    AND s.site_key IN ('093.3 026.7', '093.3 028.0', '093.3 030.0')")

mt   <- q("SELECT description, derivation FROM measurement_type WHERE measurement_type = 'mld_sigma_theta_0125'")
cr   <- q("SELECT * FROM cruise_ref WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE}")
n_st <- n_distinct(d_sta$site_key)
k <- list(
  top_anom   = top$anom,  top_v = top$v, top_clim = top$clim_mean, top_n = top$n_cruises,
  top_site   = top$site_key, top_bin = top$depth_bin, top_date = as.Date(top$datetime),
  top_km     = round((top$station - 26.4) * KM_PER_STATION),
  prev_anom  = prev$anom, prev_cruise = prev$cruise_key,
  l50        = lay("0-50 m")$anom,   l50_n  = lay("0-50 m")$n_sta,   l50_prev  = runner("0-50 m"),
  l200       = lay("50-200 m")$anom, l200_n = lay("50-200 m")$n_sta, l200_prev = runner("50-200 m"),
  feb98      = lay("0-50 m", "1998-02-31JD")$anom,
  sal        = range(d_sal$sal), sal_anom = range(d_sal$sal - d_sal$clim),
  mld        = range(d_mld$mld), mld_clim = range(d_mld$clim))
stopifnot(top$site_key == "093.3 030.0", top$depth_bin == 40, nrow(cr) == 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: ts-events
#| include: false
# temperature and salinity departures of every cruise over the inner-Bight stations, upper 50 m, against the BOTTLE
# series' normals (quality-controlled; the CTD salinity normal carries unflagged spikes). Bottle casts through 2021;
# the fall 2026 cruise from its CTD, whose salinity matches the bottles drawn on board (see "Bottles").
# a station counts when at least three of its five 10 m bins have a value and a normal; a cruise when 8 stations do
d_tsx_all <- q("
  WITH o AS (
    SELECT cruise_key, CASE WHEN measurement_type LIKE 'salinity%' THEN 'S' ELSE 'T' END AS var, site_key, depth_bin,
           any_value(cruise_month) AS m, avg(value) AS v
    FROM obs_env
    WHERE qual_ok AND depth_bin <= 40 AND site_key IN ({inner$site_key*})
      AND ((dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'   AND measurement_type IN ('temperature', 'salinity'))
        OR (dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr') AND cruise_key = {CRUISE}))
    GROUP BY ALL),
  a AS (
    SELECT o.cruise_key, o.var, o.site_key,
           count(c.clim_mean)   AS bins,   avg(o.v - c.clim_mean)   AS anom,      -- against the monthly normal
           count(c.season_mean) AS bins_s, avg(o.v - c.season_mean) AS anom_s     -- against the seasonal normal
    FROM o JOIN climatology c
      ON c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle' AND c.measurement_type = CASE o.var WHEN 'S' THEN 'salinity' ELSE 'temperature' END
     AND c.site_key = o.site_key AND c.depth_bin = o.depth_bin AND c.month = o.m
    GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT a.cruise_key, r.year, r.cruise_month,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'T' AND bins >= 3) AS n_t, avg(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'T' AND bins >= 3) AS t_anom,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S' AND bins >= 3) AS n_s, avg(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S' AND bins >= 3) AS s_anom,
         min(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S' AND bins >= 3) AS s_min, max(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S' AND bins >= 3) AS s_max,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S' AND bins_s >= 3) AS n_ss, avg(anom_s) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S' AND bins_s >= 3) AS s_season
  FROM a JOIN cruise_ref r USING (cruise_key) GROUP BY ALL")
d_tss   <- d_tsx_all |> filter(n_ss >= 8) |> arrange(desc(s_season))        # by the seasonal normal: more cruises
d_tsx   <- d_tsx_all |> filter(n_t >= 8, n_s >= 8)                          # by the monthly normal
tsx     <- function(cruise) d_tsx |> filter(cruise_key == cruise)
fs0     <- function(x, d = 2) if (abs(x) < 0.5 * 10^-d) f1(0, d) else fs(x, d)   # a departure that rounds to zero carries no sign
ts26    <- tsx(CRUISE)
ts_prev <- d_tsx |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice_max(s_anom, n = 1)
stopifnot(
  nrow(ts26) == 1, ts26$s_anom > ts_prev$s_anom, ts_prev$cruise_key == "1998-02-31JD", abs(tsx("2015-11-32OC")$s_anom) < 0.05,
  d_tss$cruise_key[1:2] == c(CRUISE, "1998-02-31JD"), nrow(d_tss) > nrow(d_tsx), "1997-09-32NM" %in% d_tss$cruise_key)   # the seasonal normal gives the same order
```

::: {.callout-important title="Preliminary data"}
The measurements from this cruise are **preliminary**: processed at sea, before final calibration
(`data_stage` `r cr$ctd_stage` in release `r VER`). This analysis has not been peer reviewed. The checks under
[Is it real?](#sec-checks) are why the headline numbers are stated with confidence; their second decimal may change.
:::

## Summary {.unnumbered}

CalCOFI has measured the ocean off California at the same stations since 1949. Its fall 2026 cruise aboard
R/V *Sally Ride* (`r format(cr$date_min, "%e %B") |> trimws()` to `r format(cr$date_max, "%e %B %Y") |> trimws()`)
found the largest departure from normal temperature in that record.

- **The measurement.** On `r format(k$top_date, "%e %B %Y") |> trimws()`, about `r k$top_km` km off northern San
  Diego County (CalCOFI station 93.3 30.0), the water 40 to 50 m below the surface was **`r f1(k$top_v)` °C**.
  The 1993–2013 November average at that station and depth is **`r f1(k$top_clim)` °C**.
- **The record.** That departure, **`r fs(k$top_anom)` °C**, is the largest among the `r fk(d_share$n_cells)`
  station-and-depth values from `r d_share$n_cruises` cruises (`r d_share$yr0`–2026) that have a baseline to
  compare with, which means the stations CalCOFI occupies today. The previous largest was `r fs(k$prev_anom)` °C, on
  the same line in November 2015. The 1982–83 and 1997–98 El Niños peaked near +6 °C by the same measure. A cruder
  yardstick that reaches every station CalCOFI has ever occupied, the old lines off Baja California included,
  [gives the same answer](#sec-whole-record). The largest departure below the surface that a search of the
  literature found for the California Current, 8 to 8.7 °C off Baja California in October 1997
  [@lynn1998; @durazo2002], is smaller too.
- **At the surface the departure is smaller.** The sea surface was `r f1(min(inner$anom), 0)` to
  `r f1(max(inner$anom), 0)` °C warmer than normal at the `r nrow(inner)` stations of the inner Southern California
  Bight and `r f1(min(outer$anom), 0)` to `r f1(max(outer$anom), 0)` °C warmer at the `r nrow(outer)` stations
  seaward of them. The largest numbers are below the surface because the warm layer is unusually thick: water of
  25 °C reached 55 m, where a normal November is already near 12 °C.
- **Averaged over the area sampled.** Through the upper 50 m at the `r k$l50_n` stations sampled, the ocean was
  **`r f1(k$l50)` °C warmer than normal**. The previous high over those same stations was
  `r fs(k$l50_prev$anom)` °C (November 2015). At the peak of the 1997–98 El Niño it was `r fs(k$feb98)` °C.
- **It is different water.** The warm layer is also unusually salty (`r f1(k$sal[1], 2)`–`r f1(k$sal[2], 2)`, about
  `r f1(mean(k$sal_anom))` above normal): the mark of water from the subtropics, not of local water warmed in place.
  It is lighter than anything normally found at that station, and it has pressed the water beneath it about
  100 m deeper than normal, which is what makes the departures at depth so large. Over the inner Bight the upper
  50 m is `r f1(ts26$s_anom, 2)` saltier than normal; the highest any earlier cruise found there is
  `r f1(ts_prev$s_anom, 2)`, at the peak of the 1997–98 El Niño, and the warm water of 2014–15
  [was not salty at all](#sec-salt).
- **It has been checked.** The instrument's two temperature sensors agree within 0.01 °C through the warm layer,
  and its salinity matches water samples analysed on board. A buoy 2 km from one station read 25.1 °C when the
  instrument read 25.0 °C. The shore station on Scripps Pier recorded both the heat and the salt on its own
  instruments. Satellite analyses show the surface there about 5 °C above normal on the same day.
- **What it does not show.** The cruise sampled `r n_st` stations on CalCOFI's three southern lines, off Southern
  California, and says nothing about waters farther north. The measurements show how warm the water is, not why:
  NOAA reports a strong El Niño in progress on top of a marine heatwave off California since 2025, and says the two
  [cannot yet be separated](#sec-context).

::: {.callout-tip title="Describing it correctly"}
- "`r f1(k$top_anom)` °C warmer than normal" needs "**at 40 to 50 m depth**" beside it. At the sea surface the
  figure is `r f1(min(inner$anom), 0)` to `r f1(max(inner$anom), 0)` °C in the inner Southern California Bight.
- For the region, the fair figure is the layer average: **about `r f1(k$l50, 0)` °C warmer than normal through the
  upper 50 m**, against a previous record of `r f1(k$l50_prev$anom)` °C.
- "Normal" is the 1993–2013 average for November at the same station and depth.
- "The largest in CalCOFI's record" means the largest departure from that normal at the stations CalCOFI occupies
  today, in a record that begins in 1949. It is a statement about these stations, not about the Pacific.
- The data are preliminary.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-cap: "How much warmer than normal the upper 50 m of the ocean was at each station of the fall 2026 CalCOFI cruise. Dots are the stations sampled, labelled with their departure in °C. The shading between them is interpolated and stops at the outermost stations. Normal is the 1993–2013 average for November at the same station and depth. Preliminary data."
#| fig-alt: "Map of the ocean off Southern California with the stations of the cruise coloured by temperature departure. Stations inside the Southern California Bight are 7 to 10 degrees Celsius warmer than normal through the upper 50 metres; stations farther offshore are 1 to 4 degrees warmer."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.1
sf_use_s2(F)
land <- ne_countries(scale = 10, country = c("United States of America", "Mexico"), returnclass = "sf") |>
  st_crop(xmin = -127, xmax = -114, ymin = 28, ymax = 37)

pts <- d_sta |>
  filter(layer == "0-50 m", !is.na(anom)) |>
  transmute(site_key, line, station, lon, lat, z = anom)
stopifnot(min(pts$z) >= 0)   # the colour scale below starts at 0: nothing may hide under it

# the surface between the stations: the Explorer's own interpolator (ordinary kriging, calcofi4r::cc_interpolate()),
# drawn only inside the hull of the stations sampled (plus 15 km), never over land, and held inside the range of
# the measured values: the shading interpolates, it never extrapolates a gradient past the last station
srf  <- cc_interpolate(pts, method = "ok", cell_deg = 0.03, mask_km = 60, se = F)
hull <- st_as_sf(pts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_union() |> st_convex_hull() |>
  st_transform(3310) |> st_buffer(15e3) |> st_transform(4326)
r    <- cc_interpolate_rast(srf)[["value"]] |>
  project("EPSG:4326") |>
  mask(vect(hull)) |>
  mask(vect(land), inverse = T)
d_r  <- as.data.frame(r, xy = T, na.rm = T) |>
  mutate(value = pmin(pmax(value, min(pts$z)), max(pts$z)))

# labels and palette ----
pal_warm <- cmocean("balance")(256)[129:256]   # the warm half of the diverging ramp: white at 0
d_city <- tribble(
  ~name,           ~lon,     ~lat,  ~hjust,
  "San Diego",     -117.16,  32.72, -0.12,
  "Los Angeles",   -118.24,  34.05, -0.12,
  "Santa Barbara", -119.70,  34.42, -0.10)
d_line <- pts |>
  filter(line %in% c(86.7, 90, 93.3)) |>
  group_by(line) |> slice_max(station, n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = glue("line {format(line, nsmall = 1)}"))
rec <- pts |> filter(site_key == k$top_site)

# map ----
ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = d_r, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_contour(data = d_r, aes(x, y, z = value), breaks = seq(2, 8, 2), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = SAND, colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(lon, lat, fill = z), shape = 21, size = 3.4, colour = INK, stroke = 0.35) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = pts, aes(lon, lat, label = f1(z)), size = 2.9, colour = INK, seed = 1, max.overlaps = Inf,
    box.padding = 0.22, point.padding = 0.2, min.segment.length = 0.4, segment.colour = MUTED, segment.size = 0.2,
    bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.14) +
  geom_point(data = d_city, aes(lon, lat), shape = 22, size = 1.6, fill = INK, colour = INK) +
  geom_text(data = d_city, aes(lon, lat, label = name, hjust = hjust), size = 3.2, colour = INK) +
  geom_text(data = d_line, aes(lon - 0.12, lat - 0.2, label = label), size = 3, colour = MUTED, fontface = "italic", hjust = 1) +
  annotate("segment", x = -117.75, y = 31.6, xend = rec$lon - 0.01, yend = rec$lat - 0.07, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.35) +
  annotate(
    "label", x = -117.75, y = 31.6, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 3.1, colour = INK, fill = "white", label.size = 0.25,
    lineheight = 0.95, label.padding = unit(5, "pt"),
    label = glue("Station 93.3 30.0\n{f1(k$top_v)} °C at 40–50 m depth:\n{fs(k$top_anom)} °C, the largest\ndeparture on record")) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = pal_warm, limits = c(0, ANOM_MAX), breaks = seq(0, 12, 3), name = "°C above the November normal",
    guide = guide_colourbar(
      direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top", barwidth = unit(150, "pt"), barheight = unit(9, "pt"),
      frame.colour = STONE, ticks.colour = "white")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-124.9, -116.1), ylim = c(29.9, 34.9), expand = F) +
  labs(
    title    = glue("The upper 50 m of the ocean off Southern California, {trimws(format(cr$date_min, '%e %B'))} – {trimws(format(cr$date_max, '%e %B %Y'))}"),
    subtitle = glue("Temperature departure from normal, averaged over 0–50 m, at the {nrow(pts)} CalCOFI stations sampled (°C)"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = glue(
      "Normal: the 1993–2013 average for November at the same station and depth. Shading is interpolated between the stations sampled, never beyond them.\n",
      "CalCOFI CTD, R/V Sally Ride; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary data.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "#eaf1f6", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major   = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position    = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.16, 0.88),
    legend.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.25),
    legend.margin      = margin(6, 10, 6, 10),
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 9.5),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = MUTED))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-profiles
#| fig-cap: "Temperature against depth at the four inshore stations of line 93.3, off northern San Diego County. Red is the fall 2026 cast at 1 m resolution. Blue is the November normal (the 1993–2013 mean, with a band of one standard deviation). Grey lines are every other November cruise with a CTD cast at the station; gold is November 2015, the previous record. The arrow marks each station's largest measured departure from normal. Preliminary data."
#| fig-alt: "Four panels of temperature profiles from the surface to 160 metres. In every panel the 2026 profile stands far to the warm side of the normal and of every earlier November, with a uniform layer near 25 degrees Celsius reaching about 55 metres."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.6
SITES    <- c("093.3 026.7", "093.3 028.0", "093.3 030.0", "093.3 035.0")
ZMAX     <- 160
lab_site <- function(x) glue("station {as.numeric(sub('.* ', '', x))}")

d_2026 <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_m, avg(value) AS temp FROM cast_1m
  WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND direction = 'd' AND measurement_qual IS NULL
    AND site_key IN ({SITES*}) AND depth_m <= {ZMAX}
  GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY site_key, depth_m")
d_norm <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_bin + 5 AS depth_m, clim_mean AS temp, clim_sd AS sd, n_cruises FROM climatology
  WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND month = 11 AND clim_mean IS NOT NULL
    AND depth_bin IS NOT NULL AND site_key IN ({SITES*}) AND depth_bin + 5 <= {ZMAX}
  ORDER BY site_key, depth_bin")
d_prev <- q("
  SELECT site_key, cruise_key, cruise_year AS yr, depth_bin + 5 AS depth_m, v AS temp FROM cell
  WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND cruise_month = 11 AND cruise_key <> {CRUISE}
    AND site_key IN ({SITES*}) AND depth_bin + 5 <= {ZMAX}
  ORDER BY site_key, cruise_key, depth_bin")
d_peak <- d_cell26 |>
  filter(site_key %in% SITES) |>
  group_by(site_key) |> slice_max(anom, n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(depth_m = depth_bin + 5)
d_lab <- tibble(
  site_key = SITES[1], temp = 15.2, depth_m = c(96, 108, 120, 138),
  label    = c("31 Oct – 1 Nov 2026", "November 2015", "November normal\n1993–2013, ± 1 sd", "every other November"),
  col      = c(COL_2026, COL_2015, COL_NORM, STONE),
  lw       = c(1.1, 0.8, 0.9, 0.35))

ggplot(mapping = aes(temp, depth_m)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = d_norm, aes(xmin = temp - sd, xmax = temp + sd), fill = COL_NORM, alpha = 0.15, orientation = "y") +
  geom_path(data = filter(d_prev, yr != 2015), aes(group = cruise_key), colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_path(data = filter(d_prev, yr == 2015), aes(group = cruise_key), colour = COL_2015, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_path(data = d_norm, colour = COL_NORM, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_path(data = d_2026, colour = COL_2026, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_segment(
    data = d_peak, aes(x = clim_mean, xend = v, yend = depth_m), colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, "pt"), ends = "both")) +
  geom_text(data = d_peak, aes(x = (clim_mean + v) / 2, y = depth_m - 5, label = paste(fs(anom), "°C")), colour = INK, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = d_lab, aes(label = label), colour = INK, size = 3.1, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.8, lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_segment(data = d_lab, aes(x = temp - 3.4, xend = temp - 0.6, yend = depth_m), colour = d_lab$col, linewidth = d_lab$lw) +
  facet_wrap(~ site_key, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(lab_site)) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(ZMAX, 0), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, ZMAX, 20)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(9, 27.5), breaks = seq(10, 26, 4), position = "top") +
  labs(
    title    = "Line 93.3 off San Diego County: a 25 °C layer reaches 55 m, where the water is normally 12 °C",
    subtitle = glue("Temperature (°C) against depth (m), {trimws(format(min(sfc$t0[sfc$site_key %in% SITES]), '%e %B'))} – {trimws(format(max(sfc$t0[sfc$site_key %in% SITES]), '%e %B %Y'))}, beside the November normal and every other November cruise ({min(d_prev$yr)}–{max(d_prev$yr)})"),
    x = NULL, y = "Depth (m)",
    caption  = glue(
      "Normal: the 1993–2013 mean per 10 m depth bin for cruises whose month is November ({min(d_norm$n_cruises)}–{max(d_norm$n_cruises)} cruises at these stations). The arrow is each station's largest measured departure.\n",
      "CalCOFI CTD, R/V Sally Ride; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary data.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(14, "pt"))
```

## What CalCOFI measures, and what "normal" means here {#sec-background}

The California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) has occupied a fixed grid of stations off
California since 1949, four times a year in recent decades [@bograd2003calcofi; @mcclatchie2014]. At each station a CTD (an instrument that records
conductivity, temperature and depth) is lowered to about 500 m, and water is collected in bottles at about 20
depths. The stations sit on numbered lines that run offshore from the coast: line 93.3 leaves the coast north of
San Diego, line 90.0 at Dana Point and line 86.7 near Santa Monica Bay.

This page uses the CalCOFI Integrated Database, release **`r VER`** (<https://doi.org/`r CAT$doi`>), in which two
temperature series reach back through the record:

- the **CTD** series (`temperature_ave`, the average of the instrument's two sensors), `r q("SELECT min(cruise_year) AS y FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast'")$y`–2026, with a value every 10 m;
- the **bottle** series (`temperature`), `r q("SELECT min(cruise_year) AS y FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'")$y`–`r q("SELECT max(cruise_year) AS y FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'")$y`, at the bottle depths.

**Normal** is the release's own `climatology` table: for each station, each 10 m depth bin and each calendar month,
the mean of everything measured there on cruises of that month during **1993–2013**, kept only where at least five
cruises contribute. A **departure** (an anomaly) is a measurement minus the normal of its own station, depth and
month. It is the same baseline the [Explorer](https://calcofi.io/explore/) and the
[CTD transects](https://calcofi.io/ctd-transects/?line=93.3&cruise=2026-11-33P4&var=temperature_ave&mode=anomaly)
subtract. Where no normal exists a departure is left blank; it is never treated as zero.

The fall cruise does not sail in the same month every year, and that matters for what follows. "November" on this
page means the cruises whose median cast date falls in November.

## The measurement {#sec-measurement}

### Line 93.3, bin by bin

The section plot that first showed the anomaly draws contours, which are interpolated between stations. The table
below is what was measured: each 10 m depth bin at the four inshore stations of line 93.3, beside the normal for
that bin and the number of 1993–2013 November cruises the normal averages.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bins
d_bins <- d_cell26 |>
  filter(line == 93.3, station <= 35, depth_bin <= 100) |>
  arrange(station, depth_bin) |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `depth (m)` = glue("{depth_bin}–{depth_bin + 10}"),
    `observed (°C)` = round(v, 2), `normal (°C)` = round(clim_mean, 2), `normal sd` = round(clim_sd, 2),
    `baseline cruises` = n_cruises, `departure (°C)` = round(anom, 2),
    `departure from the Sep–Nov normal (°C)` = round(anom_season, 2))
dt_(d_bins, caption = "Measured 10 m bins on line 93.3, stations 26.7 to 35, fall 2026.")
```

```{r}
#| label: bins-numbers
#| include: false
st28 <- d_cell26 |> filter(site_key == "093.3 028.0") |> slice_max(anom, n = 2)
n_base <- d_cell26 |> filter(line == 93.3, station <= 35, depth_bin <= 100) |> pull(n_cruises) |> range()
top_season <- d_cell26 |> filter(!is.na(anom_season)) |> slice_max(anom_season, n = 1)
```

- **The largest measured departure is `r fs(k$top_anom, 2)` °C** (station 30, 40–50 m: `r f1(k$top_v, 2)` °C against
  `r f1(k$top_clim, 2)` °C). The next station inshore reaches `r fs(st28$anom[1], 2)` °C at `r st28$depth_bin[1]`–`r st28$depth_bin[1] + 10` m and
  `r fs(st28$anom[2], 2)` °C at `r st28$depth_bin[2]`–`r st28$depth_bin[2] + 10` m. The "12" on the contour plot is
  measured; it is not made by interpolation.
- The normal behind each bin is **`r n_base[1]` to `r n_base[2]` November cruises**.
- Against the seasonal normal (September to November, `r top_season$season_n_cruises` cruises) the largest departure
  is still **`r fs(top_season$anom_season, 2)` °C**.

```{r}
#| label: fig-section
#| fig-cap: "Line 93.3 from 175 km offshore (left) to the coast (right), surface to 200 m: the November normal, what was measured on 31 October and 1 November 2026, and the difference. Triangles mark the stations; between them the values are interpolated along the line at each depth. Isotherms every 2 °C. Blank areas are below the sea floor or below the cast. Preliminary data."
#| fig-alt: "Three stacked depth sections. The normal shows a thin warm surface layer over cold water. The 2026 section shows warm water from the surface to about 60 metres inshore. The difference peaks at 40 to 60 metres depth near the coast."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8.6
d_sec <- q("
  SELECT site_key, station, depth_bin, v AS observed, clim_mean AS normal, anom AS difference FROM cell
  WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND line = 93.3 AND depth_bin < 200
  ORDER BY station, depth_bin") |>
  mutate(km = (station - 26.4) * KM_PER_STATION, depth_m = depth_bin + 5)
d_stn  <- distinct(d_sec, station, km)
grid_x <- seq(min(d_sec$km), max(d_sec$km), by = 1)
# along the line, at each depth bin: linear between the stations that have a value there, never beyond them
along <- function(col) d_sec |>
  filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) |>
  group_by(depth_m) |> filter(n() >= 2) |>
  reframe(value = approx(km, .data[[col]], xout = grid_x, rule = 1)$y, km = grid_x) |>
  filter(!is.na(value))

sec_panel <- function(col, title, pal, lim, brk, legend, top = NULL, bottom = NULL) {
  d <- along(col)
  ggplot(d, aes(km, depth_m)) +
    geom_raster(aes(fill = value), interpolate = T) +
    geom_contour(aes(z = value), breaks = seq(-20, 40, 2), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(data = d_stn, aes(km, 0), shape = 25, size = 2, fill = INK, colour = INK, inherit.aes = F) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = pal, limits = lim, breaks = brk, oob = scales::squish, name = legend,
      guide = guide_colourbar(barheight = unit(95, "pt"), barwidth = unit(8, "pt"), frame.colour = STONE, ticks.colour = "white")) +
    scale_x_reverse(
      expand = c(0, 0), name = bottom,
      sec.axis = dup_axis(breaks = d_stn$km, labels = d_stn$station, name = top)) +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(200, -6), breaks = seq(0, 200, 50)) +
    labs(subtitle = title, y = "Depth (m)") +
    theme_story() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = MUTED),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", size = rel(0.95), margin = margin(b = 2)),
      axis.title.x.top = element_text(size = 9, colour = MUTED, hjust = 0), axis.title.x.bottom = element_text(size = 10.5),
      panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#eef0f2", colour = NA))}

pal_temp <- cmocean("thermal")(256)
p_norm <- sec_panel("normal",     "The November normal, 1993–2013",             pal_temp, c(8, 26), seq(8, 26, 6), "°C", top = "station")
p_obs  <- sec_panel("observed",   "Measured, 31 October – 1 November 2026",      pal_temp, c(8, 26), seq(8, 26, 6), "°C")
p_diff <- sec_panel("difference", "The difference: how much warmer than normal", pal_warm, c(0, ANOM_MAX), seq(0, 12, 3), "°C above\nnormal",
                    bottom = "Distance offshore along the line (km)")
stopifnot(min(d_sec$difference, na.rm = T) > -0.5)   # the warm-only scale hides nothing below zero

times <- c("twice", "three times", "four times", "five times")[floor(mean(d_mld$mld) / mean(d_mld$clim)) - 1]
p_norm / p_obs / p_diff +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = glue("Line 93.3: the warm surface layer is more than {times} its normal thickness"),
    caption = glue("CalCOFI CTD, 10 m depth bins; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary data.  calcofi.io"),
    theme   = theme_story())
```

### What kind of anomaly this is

Read the profiles before the numbers. At stations 26.7, 28 and 30 the cruise found a **mixed layer of about 25 °C
reaching `r f1(min(k$mld), 0)`–`r f1(max(k$mld), 0)` m** (by a density criterion of 0.125 kg m⁻³, one of the
standard thresholds [@levitus1982; @deboyermontegut2004]; the November normal there is
`r f1(min(k$mld_clim), 0)`–`r f1(max(k$mld_clim), 0)` m). Below it the temperature falls steeply. The
departure peaks at 40–60 m because that is where a normal November has already dropped into the cold water of the
thermocline. The sea surface was about 7 °C above normal; the thickness of the layer adds the rest.

The water is also a different water mass. Salinity in the layer is **`r f1(k$sal[1], 2)`–`r f1(k$sal[2], 2)`** at
stations 28 and 30, `r f1(k$sal_anom[1], 2)` to `r f1(k$sal_anom[2], 2)` above the November normal, where the
normal's own standard deviation is about `r f1(mean(d_sal$sd), 2)`. Warming the local surface layer does not change
its salt. [The water mass](#sec-watermass) takes this up below.

### One spot, 76 years

```{r}
#| label: fig-cell-history
#| fig-cap: "Every temperature CalCOFI has measured at 40–50 m depth at station 93.3 30.0. November cruises are in colour (open circles: bottle samples; filled: CTD); every other month is grey. The line is the 1993–2013 November normal. Preliminary data for 2026."
#| fig-alt: "Scatter of temperature against year at one station and depth from 1950 to 2026. Values lie between 10 and 18 degrees Celsius in every month and year, except a single point at 25 degrees in 2026."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.3
d_hist <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, dataset_key, cruise_year, cruise_month, datetime, v, anom, clim_mean FROM cell
  WHERE site_key = {k$top_site} AND depth_bin = {k$top_bin}") |>
  mutate(
    date   = as.Date(datetime),
    series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"),
    nov    = cruise_month == 11)
h_prev <- d_hist |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice_max(v, n = 1, with_ties = F)
h_lab  <- bind_rows(
  d_hist |> filter(cruise_key == CRUISE) |> mutate(label = glue("{format(date, '%e %b %Y') |> trimws()}: {f1(v)} °C")),
  h_prev |> mutate(label = glue("{format(date, '%e %b %Y') |> trimws()}: {f1(v)} °C")))

ggplot(d_hist, aes(date, v)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = k$top_clim, colour = COL_NORM, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, !nov), colour = STONE, size = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  annotate("label", x = as.Date("1968-06-01"), y = k$top_clim, label = glue("November normal {f1(k$top_clim)} °C"), colour = INK, fill = "white", size = 3.2, linewidth = 0, border.colour = NA) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, nov), aes(shape = series), colour = COL_NORM, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, cruise_key == CRUISE), colour = COL_2026, size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(data = h_lab, aes(label = label), colour = INK, size = 3.4, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -500, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(bottle = 1, CTD = 16)) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(seq(1950, 2020, 10), "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 26, 4)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Station 93.3 30.0, 40–50 m depth: nothing like it in any month since 1950",
    subtitle = glue("Temperature (°C) on {n_distinct(d_hist$cruise_key)} cruises. Colour: November cruises (open: bottle, filled: CTD). Grey: every other month."),
    x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_story()
```

Across all months, `r n_distinct(d_hist$cruise_key)` cruises since `r min(d_hist$cruise_year)` have sampled this
depth at this station. The warmest before this cruise was `r f1(h_prev$v, 2)` °C
(`r trimws(format(h_prev$date, "%e %B %Y"))`, on the November 2015 cruise).

## Is it real? {#sec-checks}

A 12.8 °C departure is the first thing an oceanographer will challenge. These are the checks, from the instrument
outward.

### The data's stage and its quality flags

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flags
d_stage <- q("
  SELECT data_stage, count(*) AS casts FROM sample
  WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND sample_type = 'cast' GROUP BY ALL")
d_flag <- q("
  SELECT f.measurement_type, f.measurement_qual AS flag, count(*) AS values, count(DISTINCT f.sample_key) AS casts,
         min(f.depth_min_m) AS depth_min_m, max(f.depth_min_m) AS depth_max_m,
         string_agg(DISTINCT s.site_key, ', ' ORDER BY s.site_key) AS stations
  FROM obs_ctd_full f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE f.measurement_qual IS NOT NULL AND f.measurement_type LIKE 'temperature%'
  GROUP BY ALL")
n_prelim <- q("SELECT count(*) AS n, min(cruise_key) AS first FROM cruise_ref WHERE ctd_stage LIKE 'preliminary%'")
kable(d_flag, caption = "Every flagged temperature value on the cruise (CTD codes: 8 questionable, 9 bad or missing).")
```

All `r sum(d_stage$casts)` casts of the cruise (`r n_st` stations, down and up) carry `data_stage`
**`r paste(d_stage$data_stage, collapse = ", ")`**: one-metre averages processed at sea, before final calibration.
So does every CTD cruise since `r n_prelim$first` in this release (`r n_prelim$n` cruises). The only flagged
temperatures are on one up cast, on the primary sensor, and the sensor-pair average the analysis uses already leaves
them out. Nothing on line 93.3 is flagged.

### Two sensors, two passes

```{r}
#| label: chk-sensors
d_pair <- q("
  SELECT a.site_key, a.direction, a.depth_m, a.value AS t1, b.value AS t2
  FROM cast_1m a JOIN cast_1m b USING (sample_key, depth_m)
  WHERE a.measurement_type = 'temperature_1' AND b.measurement_type = 'temperature_2'
    AND a.measurement_qual IS NULL AND b.measurement_qual IS NULL")
d_du <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_m, max(value) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'd') AS down, max(value) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'u') AS up
  FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL GROUP BY ALL") |>
  filter(!is.na(down), !is.na(up))
d_gap <- q("
  SELECT site_key, date_diff('minute', min(datetime) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'd'), max(datetime) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'u')) AS minutes
  FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND depth_m <= 40 AND site_key IN ({core*}) GROUP BY site_key")
chk <- list(
  pair_all  = d_pair |> filter(depth_m <= 100) |> summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(t1 - t2), p99 = quantile(abs(t1 - t2), 0.99)),
  pair_core = d_pair |> filter(site_key %in% core, depth_m <= 50) |> summarize(n = n(), max = max(abs(t1 - t2)), median = median(abs(t1 - t2))),
  du_core   = d_du   |> filter(site_key %in% core, depth_m <= 40) |> summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(abs(down - up)), max = max(abs(down - up))),
  du_base   = d_du   |> filter(site_key %in% core, between(depth_m, 50, 65)) |> summarize(max = max(abs(down - up))),
  gap       = range(d_gap$minutes))
```

The CTD carries two independent temperature sensors. Through the warm layer at stations 28 and 30 (the top 50 m,
`r chk$pair_core$n` one-metre values) they never differ by more than **`r f1(chk$pair_core$max, 3)` °C**; half of
the values differ by `r f1(chk$pair_core$median * 1000, 1)` thousandths of a degree or less. Over every cast of the
cruise, in the top 100 m, their mean difference is `r f1(chk$pair_all$mean, 4)` °C.

Each station is also measured twice, on the way down and on the way up. At those two stations the two passes
through the top 40 m are `r chk$gap[1]` to `r chk$gap[2]` minutes apart and differ by `r f1(chk$du_core$mean, 2)` °C
on average. At the base of the layer (50–65 m) they differ by up to `r f1(chk$du_base$max, 1)` °C: internal waves
lift and drop that boundary by a few metres within the hour. That moves the 50–60 m bin. It does not move the
40–50 m bin, which lies inside the layer on both passes.

### Bottles: salinity and oxygen

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bottles
d_btl <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_m,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave')   AS t,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'salinity_1')        AS s_ctd,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'salinity_btl')      AS s_btl,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'sigma_theta_1')     AS sigma,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'oxygen_btl_ml_l')   AS o2_btl
  FROM cast_1m WHERE direction = 'u' AND site_key IN ({core*}) AND depth_m <= 60
  GROUP BY ALL HAVING s_btl IS NOT NULL OR o2_btl IS NOT NULL ORDER BY site_key, depth_m") |>
  left_join(
    d_cell26 |> transmute(site_key, depth_bin, t_normal = clim_mean),
    by = join_by(site_key, closest(depth_m >= depth_bin))) |>
  mutate(
    # oxygen solubility (Garcia & Gordon 1992, via gsw), umol/kg -> mL/L
    o2_sat        = gsw_O2sol_SP_pt(s_ctd, t)        * (1000 + sigma) / 1000 / 44.66,
    o2_sat_normal = gsw_O2sol_SP_pt(s_ctd, t_normal) * (1000 + sigma) / 1000 / 44.66)
d_btl |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `depth (m)` = depth_m, `CTD temperature (°C)` = round(t, 2),
    `CTD salinity` = round(s_ctd, 3), `bottle salinity` = round(s_btl, 3), difference = round(s_btl - s_ctd, 3),
    `bottle oxygen (mL/L)` = round(o2_btl, 2), `saturation at the measured temperature` = round(o2_sat, 2),
    `saturation at the normal temperature` = round(o2_sat_normal, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Water samples from the warm layer at stations 28 and 30, beside the CTD on the up cast.")
```

```{r}
#| label: bottles-numbers
#| include: false
# what a 0.1 °C temperature error would do to salinity computed from the same conductivity (in the warm layer)
ds_01 <- with(list(s = mean(k$sal), t = 25, p = 30), gsw_SP_from_C(gsw_C_from_SP(s, t, p), t + 0.1, p) - s)
btl <- list(
  ds     = max(abs(d_btl$s_btl - d_btl$s_ctd), na.rm = T),
  o2     = range(d_btl$o2_btl[d_btl$depth_m <= 50], na.rm = T),
  o2_sat = mean(d_btl$o2_sat[d_btl$depth_m <= 50 & !is.na(d_btl$o2_btl)]),
  o2_nrm = mean(d_btl$o2_sat_normal[d_btl$depth_m <= 50 & !is.na(d_btl$o2_btl)]))
```

Salinity is measured twice by unrelated methods: the CTD computes it from conductivity **and temperature**, and a
salinometer measures it on the bottled water samples in the ship's laboratory. In the warm layer the two agree to
within **`r f1(btl$ds, 3)`**. A temperature error of only 0.1 °C would shift the CTD's salinity by
`r f1(abs(ds_01), 2)` and break that agreement; an error of several degrees is out of the question.

The oxygen titrated from the same bottles (`r f1(btl$o2[1], 2)`–`r f1(btl$o2[2], 2)` mL/L down to 50 m) is what a
mixed layer in contact with the air holds at 25 °C (saturation `r f1(btl$o2_sat, 2)` mL/L). Water at the normal
temperature of those depths would hold about `r f1(btl$o2_nrm, 1)` mL/L.

### The baseline: is the normal the right normal?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-baseline
# the record cell against every reasonable definition of its normal
b_cells <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, cruise_year, v, n_obs FROM cell
  WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND site_key = {k$top_site} AND depth_bin = {k$top_bin} AND cruise_month = 11 AND cruise_key <> {CRUISE}")
b_in  <- b_cells |> filter(between(cruise_year, 1993, 2013))
b_loo <- map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(b_in)), \(i) with(b_in[-i, ], sum(v * n_obs) / sum(n_obs)))
b_btl <- q("
  SELECT clim_mean, n_cruises FROM climatology
  WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle' AND site_key = {k$top_site} AND depth_bin = {k$top_bin} AND month = 11")
# the same baseline cruises from their FULL one-metre casts (obs_ctd_full), not the thinned series the normal is built from
release_view("obs_ctd_full", parts = b_in$cruise_key, name = "obs_ctd_full_base")
b_full <- q("
  SELECT f.cruise_key, avg(f.measurement_value) AS v, count(*) AS n
  FROM obs_ctd_full_base f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE f.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND f.measurement_qual IS NULL AND s.site_key = {k$top_site}
    AND f.depth_min_m >= {k$top_bin} AND f.depth_min_m < {k$top_bin + 10}
  GROUP BY f.cruise_key")
stopifnot(nrow(b_full) == nrow(b_in))
# fall 2026 from its own one-metre casts, for the row that uses one-metre normals (like with like)
v26_full <- q("
  SELECT avg(value) AS v FROM cast_1m
  WHERE site_key = {k$top_site} AND measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL
    AND depth_m >= {k$top_bin} AND depth_m < {k$top_bin + 10}")$v
d_base <- tribble(
  ~`definition of normal`,                                                             ~cruises,                ~normal,          ~value,
  "the release's climatology: every 1993–2013 November value in the bin (used on this page)", top$n_cruises,     top$clim_mean,    top$v,
  "the same cruises, one value per cruise",                                            nrow(b_in),               mean(b_in$v),     top$v,
  "the same cruises and fall 2026 from their full one-metre casts, not the thinned series", nrow(b_full),        mean(b_full$v),   v26_full,
  "leaving out each baseline cruise in turn: the lowest normal",                       nrow(b_in) - 1L,          min(b_loo),       top$v,
  "leaving out each baseline cruise in turn: the highest normal",                      nrow(b_in) - 1L,          max(b_loo),       top$v,
  "every earlier November cruise with a CTD cast, to 2025, one value per cruise",      nrow(b_cells),            mean(b_cells$v),  top$v,
  "the bottle series' own climatology for the cell",                                   b_btl$n_cruises,          b_btl$clim_mean,  top$v,
  "the release's seasonal normal (September to November)",                             top$season_n_cruises,     top$season_mean,  top$v) |>
  mutate(`normal (°C)` = round(normal, 2), `fall 2026 (°C)` = round(value, 2), `departure (°C)` = round(value - normal, 2)) |>
  select(-normal, -value)
kable(d_base, caption = glue("The departure at the record cell (station 93.3 30.0, 40–50 m) under {nrow(d_base)} definitions of normal."))
```

```{r}
#| label: baseline-numbers
#| include: false
d_when <- q("
  SELECT DISTINCT cruise_key, CAST(datetime AS DATE) AS date FROM cell
  WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND cruise_month = 11 AND cruise_year BETWEEN 1993 AND 2013
    AND line = 93.3 AND station <= 35 AND depth_bin = 0")
doy <- function(d) as.integer(format(d, "%j")) - as.integer(format(as.Date(paste0(format(d, "%Y"), "-11-01")), "%j"))
w   <- list(n = n_distinct(d_when$cruise_key), first = min(doy(d_when$date)), last = max(doy(d_when$date)), mid = median(doy(d_when$date)))
day_of <- function(x) format(as.Date("2026-11-01") + x, "%e %B") |> trimws()
base_rng <- range(as.numeric(d_base[[ncol(d_base)]]))
```

The normal is thin, `r top$n_cruises` cruises at this cell, so the table asks how much the answer depends on it.
Under every definition the departure is between **`r f1(base_rng[1])` and `r f1(base_rng[2])` °C**.

Timing within the season is the other way a baseline can mislead. The cruise worked the inshore end of line 93.3 on
31 October and 1 November. The `r w$n` cruises behind the November normal there were on station between
`r day_of(w$first)` and `r day_of(w$last)` (median `r day_of(w$mid)`), so the cruise sits inside their range, about
`r abs(w$mid) + 1` days ahead of its middle. The surface normal falls by about 2 °C from October to November, so the
calendar can account for a few tenths of a degree at the surface, not more. The seasonal normal in the last row
is the conservative bound.

### The thinned series against the full profile

The release's main table keeps a thinned CTD series (a value every 10 m plus the points where the profile bends),
and the normal was built from the same series. The check is whether a 10 m bin mean of the thinned series stands
for the full one-metre profile.

```{r}
#| label: chk-thin
d_thin <- q("
  WITH f AS (
    SELECT site_key, CAST(floor(depth_m / 10) * 10 AS INTEGER) AS depth_bin, avg(value) AS v_full
    FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL AND direction = 'd' GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT c.site_key, c.depth_bin, c.v, f.v_full, c.v - f.v_full AS diff
  FROM cell c JOIN f USING (site_key, depth_bin) WHERE c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND c.depth_bin < 200")
thin <- d_thin |> summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(diff), p95 = quantile(abs(diff), 0.95), max = max(abs(diff)))
thin_top <- d_thin |> filter(site_key == k$top_site, depth_bin == k$top_bin)
```

Over the `r thin$n` bins of the cruise above 200 m, the thinned bin mean differs from the full down-cast mean by
`r fs(thin$mean, 2)` °C on average, and by less than `r f1(thin$p95, 2)` °C in 95 % of bins (the largest
differences are in the thermocline, where a few points stand for a steep gradient). At the record cell the two
are `r f1(thin_top$v, 2)` and `r f1(thin_top$v_full, 2)` °C.

```{r}
#| label: chk-thin-baseline
# the same comparison on the six baseline cruises read at one metre, at the cruise's stations, bins 10 to 40 m
d_thinb <- q("
  WITH f AS (
    SELECT o.cruise_key, s.site_key, CAST(floor(o.depth_min_m / 10) * 10 AS INTEGER) AS depth_bin, avg(o.measurement_value) AS v_full
    FROM obs_ctd_full_base o JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
    WHERE o.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND o.measurement_qual IS NULL AND o.depth_min_m < 50 GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT c.depth_bin, count(*) AS cells, avg(c.v - f.v_full) AS thinned_minus_1m, avg(c.depth_m - c.depth_bin) AS m_below_bin_top
  FROM cell c JOIN f USING (cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin)
  WHERE c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND c.depth_bin BETWEEN 10 AND 40 AND c.site_key IN ({unique(d_sta$site_key)*})
  GROUP BY c.depth_bin ORDER BY c.depth_bin")
```

In stratified water the thinned bin mean runs a little warm. In the six baseline cruises read at one metre, at these
stations, it is `r f1(min(d_thinb$thinned_minus_1m), 2)` to `r f1(max(d_thinb$thinned_minus_1m), 2)` °C warmer than the
one-metre bin mean in the bins between 10 and 50 m, because its points sit `r f1(mean(d_thinb$m_below_bin_top))` m below
the top of the bin on average where a one-metre series sits 4.5 m. The normal is built from that same thinned
series, so a departure on this page compares like with like. A departure computed from one-metre values against
this normal reads low by that amount in ordinary, stratified years; in fall 2026, when the upper 50 m was mixed,
the two agree.

### Are the stations where they should be?

```{r}
#| label: chk-position
d_pos <- q("
  WITH h AS (
    SELECT site_key, median(latitude) AS lat0, median(longitude) AS lon0, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n_cruises
    FROM cell WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} AND depth_bin = 0 GROUP BY site_key)
  SELECT c.site_key, c.latitude, c.longitude, h.lat0, h.lon0, h.n_cruises
  FROM cell c JOIN h USING (site_key) WHERE c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND c.depth_bin = 0") |>
  mutate(km = as.numeric(st_distance(
    st_as_sf(pick(longitude, latitude), coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326),
    st_as_sf(pick(lon0, lat0), coords = c("lon0", "lat0"), crs = 4326), by_element = T)) / 1000)
```

A cast filed under the wrong station would be compared with the wrong normal. Each of the cruise's
`r nrow(d_pos)` stations with a history lies within **`r f1(max(d_pos$km))` km** of the median position of every
earlier occupation of that station (median `r f1(median(d_pos$km), 2)` km).

### Buoys

```{r}
#| label: outside-casts
# the cast list the outside-sources script reads: one row per station, from the release
d_casts <- q("
  WITH c AS (
    SELECT sample_key, site_key, min(datetime) AS t0, avg(latitude) AS lat, avg(longitude) AS lon,
           avg(value) FILTER (WHERE depth_m <= 3) AS t_top3m, avg(value) FILTER (WHERE depth_m < 10) AS t_0_10m, max(depth_m) AS zmax
    FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL AND direction = 'd' GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT site_key, replace(sample_key, 'calcofi_ctd-cast:cast:', '') AS cast_id, strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ') AS time_utc,
         round(lat, 4) AS lat, round(lon, 4) AS lon, round(t_top3m, 3) AS ctd_t_top3m, round(t_0_10m, 3) AS ctd_t_0_10m, zmax
  FROM c ORDER BY t0")
write_csv(d_casts, file.path(DIR_DATA, "casts.csv"), na = "")

# the outside sources are fetched once by scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py (NDBC keeps 45 days only)
# and kept in the repo; a missing file means that script has not been run
f_out <- file.path(DIR_DATA, c("buoy_stations.csv", "buoys_at_casts.csv", "buoy_series.csv", "satellite_at_casts.csv", "argo_profiles.csv", "sources.csv", "pier_daily.csv", "glider_index.csv"))
stopifnot("run scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py first" = all(file.exists(f_out)))
buoy_name <- function(x) str_remove(x, ",? CA\\b.*$") |> str_to_title()   # "Torrey Pines Outer, CA (100)" -> "Torrey Pines Outer"
d_bstn  <- read_csv(f_out[1]) |> mutate(name = buoy_name(name))
d_bpair <- read_csv(f_out[2]) |> mutate(buoy_name = buoy_name(buoy_name))
d_bser  <- read_csv(f_out[3]) |> mutate(time = as.POSIXct(hour_utc, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ", tz = "UTC"))
d_sat   <- read_csv(f_out[4])
d_argo  <- read_csv(f_out[5])
d_osrc  <- read_csv(f_out[6])
d_pier  <- read_csv(f_out[7]) |> mutate(yr = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")), md = format(date, "%m-%d"))
d_gl    <- read_csv(f_out[8], col_types = "cd") |> mutate(date = as.Date(paste0(month, "-15")))
```

Moored buoys report water temperature near the surface every half hour, through the National Data Buoy Center.
They are operated by other programs (most of these by the Coastal Data Information Program at Scripps [@cdip]) and
share nothing with the ship's instruments. The table pairs each cast with every buoy within 15 km, at the buoy report
nearest in time.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-buoys
d_bpair |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `cast (UTC)` = sub("T", " ", sub(":\\d\\dZ$", "", cast_time_utc)),
    `CTD, top 3 m (°C)` = round(ctd_t_top3m, 2), buoy = glue("{buoy_name} ({buoy})"), `km apart` = km_apart,
    `buoy (°C)` = buoy_wtmp, `buoy − CTD (°C)` = buoy_minus_ctd,
    `buoy range, ±12 h (°C)` = glue("{buoy_24h_min}–{buoy_24h_max}")) |>
  kable(caption = "Buoy water temperature beside the CTD (buoys report to 0.1 °C).")
```

```{r}
#| label: buoys-numbers
#| include: false
b_near  <- d_bpair |> group_by(site_key) |> slice_min(km_apart, n = 1, with_ties = F) |> ungroup()
b_best  <- d_bpair |> slice_min(km_apart, n = 1, with_ties = F)
b_cool  <- b_near |> slice_min(buoy_wtmp, n = 1, with_ties = F)
```

The closest pair is `r f1(b_best$km_apart)` km and a few minutes apart: the `r b_best$buoy_name` buoy read
**`r f1(b_best$buoy_wtmp)` °C** when the CTD read **`r f1(b_best$ctd_t_top3m, 2)` °C** at station
`r b_best$site_key`. The buoy nearest each of `r nrow(b_near)` casts (`r f1(min(b_near$km_apart), 0)`–`r f1(max(b_near$km_apart), 0)` km away)
reads within `r f1(max(abs(b_near$buoy_minus_ctd)), 1)` °C of the CTD, including the cool side of the front
(`r f1(b_cool$buoy_wtmp)` °C at `r b_cool$buoy_name` against the CTD's `r f1(b_cool$ctd_t_top3m, 2)` °C). Pairs
farther apart differ by up to `r f1(max(abs(d_bpair$buoy_minus_ctd)), 1)` °C, which is the front itself.

```{r}
#| label: fig-buoys
#| fig-cap: "Hourly water temperature at four buoys over the 45 days NDBC keeps, with the CTD's near-surface temperature at the nearest cast (white dots). The two inshore buoys sat at 24–25 °C for weeks before and after the cruise; the two offshore buoys stayed near 19–20 °C."
#| fig-alt: "Four time series from late September to mid November 2026. Two inshore buoys vary between 22 and 25.5 degrees Celsius; two offshore buoys between 19 and 22."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
SHOW <- c("46225", "46254", "46219", "46047")
d_b  <- d_bser |> filter(buoy %in% SHOW) |>
  left_join(select(d_bstn, buoy, name), by = "buoy") |>
  mutate(buoy = factor(buoy, SHOW))
col_b  <- setNames(c("#b3261e", "#c69214", "#00629b", "#457a1c"), SHOW)
d_end  <- d_b |> group_by(buoy, name) |> slice_max(time, n = 1) |> ungroup()
d_ctd  <- d_bpair |> filter(buoy %in% SHOW) |> group_by(buoy) |> slice_min(km_apart, n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(time = as.POSIXct(cast_time_utc, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"), buoy = factor(buoy, SHOW))

ggplot(d_b, aes(time, wtmp, colour = buoy)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = as.POSIXct(cr$date_min, tz = "UTC"), xmax = as.POSIXct(cr$date_max + 1, tz = "UTC"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = SAND) +
  annotate("text", x = as.POSIXct(cr$date_min, tz = "UTC") + 3.5 * 86400, y = 26.2, label = "the cruise", colour = MUTED, size = 3.1) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = d_ctd, aes(y = ctd_t_top3m), shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = INK, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = d_end, aes(label = name), colour = INK, hjust = 0, direction = "y", nudge_x = 1.2 * 86400, size = 3.2,
    segment.colour = MUTED, segment.size = 0.2, min.segment.length = 0, seed = 1, xlim = c(max(d_b$time) + 86400, NA)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_b) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "1 week", date_labels = "%e %b", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.22))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(18, 26, 2)) +
  labs(
    title    = "The warm water was there for weeks, and the cool water offshore stayed cool",
    subtitle = "Water temperature (°C), hourly means. White dots: the CTD's top 3 m at the nearest cast.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Buoy data from CDIP, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (cdip.ucsd.edu), and NOAA National Data Buoy Center, through NDBC realtime files, read 13 November 2026.") +
  theme_story()
```

### Scripps Pier

The shore station on Scripps Pier in La Jolla has its own instruments in the water at the coast and reports
temperature and salinity every few minutes (the SCCOOS automated shore station, running since 2013). These are its
daily means, of the values that pass the station's own quality tests. The pier's much longer manual record, kept
daily since 1916 [@shorestations_data; @rasmussen2020], is taken up under [context](#sec-context).

```{r}
#| label: fig-pier
#| fig-cap: "Daily mean temperature and salinity at the Scripps Pier automated shore station from 1 August to 12 November: 2026 in red, over the range of the same calendar day in every earlier year of the record (grey band, 2013–2025) and its median (grey line). The cruise is the shaded week."
#| fig-alt: "Two time series. Pier temperature in 2026 runs above the earlier range from late October and reaches 24 degrees Celsius in early November, when earlier years were at 16 to 20. Pier salinity in 2026 jumps from 33.6 to 34.25 in the week of the cruise, above anything in the earlier range."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.6
WIN <- c("08-01", "11-12")
p_long <- d_pier |>
  filter(md >= WIN[1], md <= WIN[2], md != "02-29") |>
  pivot_longer(c(temp, sal), names_to = "var", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(day = as.Date(paste0("2026-", md)), var = factor(var, c("temp", "sal"), c("Temperature (°C)", "Salinity")))
p_rng <- p_long |> filter(yr < 2026) |> group_by(var, day) |>
  summarize(lo = min(value), hi = max(value), mid = median(value), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |> filter(n >= 8)
p_26  <- p_long |> filter(yr == 2026)

pier_panel <- function(v, ylim, breaks) {
  ggplot(filter(p_26, var == v), aes(day)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = cr$date_min, xmax = cr$date_max + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = SAND) +
    geom_ribbon(data = filter(p_rng, var == v), aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = STONE, alpha = 0.45) +
    geom_line(data = filter(p_rng, var == v), aes(y = mid), colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(aes(y = value), colour = COL_2026, linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%e %b", expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = breaks) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) +          # the band may leave the axis: a few earlier days dip far below it
    labs(subtitle = v, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_story() +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", size = rel(0.95), margin = margin(b = 2)))}
s_low    <- p_rng |> filter(var == "Salinity") |> pull(lo) |> min()
s_low_26 <- p_26  |> filter(var == "Salinity") |> slice_min(value, n = 1, with_ties = F)

(pier_panel("Temperature (°C)", c(14, 26), seq(14, 26, 4)) + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())) /
  pier_panel("Salinity", c(32.8, 34.4), seq(33, 34.4, 0.4)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "At Scripps Pier, on other instruments: the same heat and the same salt",
    subtitle = glue("Daily means. Red: 2026. Grey: the range and median of the same calendar day, {min(d_pier$yr)}–2025."),
    caption  = glue(
      "The salinity axis is cut at 32.8: the earlier range dips below it on some days (to {f1(s_low)}), and so does 2026 in late August (to {f1(s_low_26$value)} on {trimws(format(s_low_26$day, '%e %B'))}).\n",
      "SCCOOS automated shore station, Scripps Pier (Scripps Institution of Oceanography), through the IOOS sensors ERDDAP, read 13 November 2026."),
    theme    = theme_story())
```

```{r}
#| label: pier-numbers
#| include: false
pier_day <- function(md_) {
  x <- d_pier |> filter(md == md_)
  list(t26 = x$temp[x$yr == 2026], s26 = x$sal[x$yr == 2026],
       t_prev = max(x$temp[x$yr < 2026], na.rm = T), t_prev_yr = x$yr[x$yr < 2026][which.max(x$temp[x$yr < 2026])],
       s_prev = max(x$sal[x$yr < 2026], na.rm = T), n_prev = sum(x$yr < 2026 & !is.na(x$temp)))}
pk    <- d_pier |> filter(yr == 2026, md >= "10-25") |> slice_max(temp, n = 1, with_ties = F)
p_pk  <- pier_day(pk$md)
p_c0  <- pier_day(format(cr$date_min - 6, "%m-%d"))          # six days before the cruise
p_s   <- d_pier |> filter(!is.na(sal)) |> mutate(rk = min_rank(desc(sal)))
p_top <- p_s |> filter(rk <= 20)
p_all <- d_pier |> slice_max(temp, n = 1, with_ties = F)
p_q   <- quantile(d_pier$sal[d_pier$date < as.Date("2026-06-01")], c(0.5, 0.99), na.rm = T)
ctd_in <- d_casts |> filter(site_key == "093.3 026.7")
PIER   <- c(lon = -117.257, lat = 32.867)                     # the shore station (and NOS station 9410230)
km_in  <- as.numeric(st_distance(
  st_sfc(st_point(PIER), crs = 4326), st_sfc(st_point(c(ctd_in$lon, ctd_in$lat)), crs = 4326))) / 1000
s_in   <- q("SELECT avg(value) AS s FROM cast_1m WHERE site_key = '093.3 026.7' AND measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND direction = 'd' AND depth_m <= 3")$s
```

On `r trimws(format(pk$date, "%e %B"))` the pier's daily mean was **`r f1(p_pk$t26, 2)` °C**. The highest for that
calendar day in the `r p_pk$n_prev` earlier years of the record was `r f1(p_pk$t_prev, 2)` °C (`r p_pk$t_prev_yr`).
The pier's warmest day on record, `r f1(p_all$temp, 2)` °C, came in `r format(p_all$date, "%B %Y")`, in high summer.

Salinity is the sharper signal. Before June 2026 the pier's daily salinity had a median of `r f1(p_q[1], 2)` and
exceeded `r f1(p_q[2], 2)` on one day in a hundred. Six days before the cruise it read `r f1(p_c0$s26, 2)`. By
`r trimws(format(pk$date, "%e %B"))` it read **`r f1(p_pk$s26, 2)`**, and `r sum(p_top$yr == 2026 & p_top$md >= "10-31")`
of the `r nrow(p_top)` saltiest days in the whole record are from `r trimws(format(cr$date_min, "%e %B"))` onward.
The CTD at station 93.3 26.7, `r f1(km_in, 0)` km from the pier,
read `r f1(ctd_in$ctd_t_top3m, 2)` °C and `r f1(s_in, 2)` at the surface on `r trimws(format(cr$date_min, "%e %B"))`.
The salty water reached the pier during the week of the cruise.

### Satellites

Two satellite analyses of sea-surface temperature, each read at every cast's position on the cast's day: NOAA's
OISST [@huang2021; @reynolds2007] (a 0.25° blend of satellite, ship and buoy data, here in its preliminary near-real-time version, with its
own anomaly against 1971–2000) and JPL's MUR [@chin2017] (0.01°; the anomaly is NOAA CoastWatch's product against
the MUR climatology of 2003–2014).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-satellite
d_sat |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `cast (UTC)` = sub("T", " ", sub(":\\d\\dZ$", "", cast_time_utc)),
    `CTD, top 3 m (°C)` = round(ctd_t_top3m, 2), `OISST (°C)` = oisst_sst, `OISST anomaly (°C)` = oisst_anom,
    `MUR (°C)` = mur_sst, `MUR anomaly (°C)` = mur_anom) |>
  dt_(caption = "Satellite sea-surface temperature analyses at each cast. An empty cell is a value the data server did not return.")
```

```{r}
#| label: satellite-numbers
#| include: false
sat_in <- d_sat |> inner_join(select(inner, site_key, anom), by = "site_key")
s_o    <- sat_in |> filter(!is.na(oisst_anom))
s_m    <- sat_in |> filter(!is.na(mur_anom))
rng    <- function(x) glue("{f1(min(x))} to {f1(max(x))}")
sat <- list(
  n = nrow(d_sat), n_oisst = sum(!is.na(d_sat$oisst_sst)), n_mur = sum(!is.na(d_sat$mur_sst)),
  d_oisst = mean(d_sat$oisst_sst - d_sat$ctd_t_top3m, na.rm = T), d_mur = mean(d_sat$mur_sst - d_sat$ctd_t_top3m, na.rm = T),
  r_oisst = cor(d_sat$oisst_sst, d_sat$ctd_t_top3m, use = "complete.obs"))
stopifnot(nrow(s_o) >= 3)
```

Across the `r sat$n_oisst` casts with an OISST value, the analysis follows the CTD closely (correlation
`r f1(sat$r_oisst, 2)`) and reads `r f1(abs(sat$d_oisst), 1)` °C `r if (sat$d_oisst < 0) "cooler" else "warmer"` on
average, as a smoothed quarter-degree product does beside a point measurement in a warm pool with sharp edges.

At the `r nrow(s_o)` stations of the inner Bight that have one, OISST puts the surface **`r rng(s_o$oisst_anom)` °C
above its own normal**, where the CTD reads `r rng(s_o$anom)` °C above the CalCOFI normal.
`r if (nrow(s_m) >= 3) glue("MUR, at {nrow(s_m)} of those stations, reads {rng(s_m$mur_anom)} °C above its normal, where the CTD reads {rng(s_m$anom)} °C.") else ""`
The baselines differ in period and in kind, and the satellite analyses smooth the sharpest part of the warm pool;
they agree with the CTD on the size of the event at the surface.
`r if (sat$n_oisst < sat$n || sat$n_mur < sat$n) glue("The data server returned OISST for {sat$n_oisst} and MUR for {sat$n_mur} of the {sat$n} casts when this page was built; the rest are empty in the table.") else ""`

### Argo floats

```{r}
#| label: tbl-argo
at_p <- function(p, t, target) { i <- which.min(abs(p - target)); if (abs(p[i] - target) <= 8) t[i] else NA_real_ }
d_ap <- d_argo |>
  group_by(float = platform_number, cycle = cycle_number, time, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarize(
    `5 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 5), `30 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 30), `50 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 50),
```
