```{r}
    `75 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 75), `100 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 100), salinity_5m = at_p(pres, psal, 5), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    km_all   = list(as.numeric(st_distance(
      st_sfc(st_point(c(longitude, latitude)), crs = 4326),
      st_as_sf(d_casts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326))) / 1000),
    `nearest station` = d_casts$site_key[which.min(km_all)], `km to it` = round(min(km_all)),
    `CTD there, top 3 m` = d_casts$ctd_t_top3m[which.min(km_all)],
    km_inner = round(min(km_all[d_casts$site_key %in% inner$site_key]))) |>
  ungroup() |> select(-km_all) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time), latitude = round(latitude, 2), longitude = round(longitude, 2)) |>
  select(float, cycle, date, latitude, longitude, `5 m`:`100 m`, salinity_5m, `nearest station`, `km to it`, `CTD there, top 3 m`, km_inner) |>
  arrange(date)
km_inner <- min(d_ap$km_inner)
d_ap     <- select(d_ap, -km_inner)
stopifnot(km_inner > 25)   # no float sampled the inner Bight
kable(d_ap, digits = 2, caption = "Argo float profiles in and around the cruise's area, two weeks before it to a week after (temperature in °C at the pressure nearest each depth).")
```

`r n_distinct(d_ap$float)` Argo floats [@wong2020; @argo_gdac] surfaced in the area around the cruise. All were over the outer part of the
grid or beyond it: none came closer than `r min(d_ap[["km to it"]])` km to a station, or than `r km_inner` km to a
station of the inner Bight. They show the offshore structure the cruise found there (surface layers of `r f1(min(d_ap[["5 m"]], na.rm = T))`–`r f1(max(d_ap[["5 m"]], na.rm = T))` °C
with salinity near `r f1(median(d_ap$salinity_5m, na.rm = T), 1)`), and so confirm the cool side of the front.
The subsurface of the warm pool itself rests on the CTD's own redundancy: two sensors, two passes, the bottle
salinities and the oxygen.

### Verdict

Not an artifact. The normal is the right one (same station, same depth, the cruise's own month, and the answer
barely moves under `r nrow(d_base) - 1` other definitions). The instrument agrees with itself, with the bottles, with the buoys
beside it, with the shore station on Scripps Pier and with the satellite analyses.

## Where it ranks {#sec-rank}

The same departure was computed for every cruise, station and 10 m depth bin in the release: the CTD series
(`r q("SELECT count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast'")$n` cruises) and the
bottle series (`r q("SELECT count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'")$n`
cruises), each against its own climatology. Of the `r n_cruises_all` cruises, `r d_share$n_cruises` have at least
one value with a normal to compare with ([why not all](#sec-caveats)).

### Single measurements

```{r}
#| label: tbl-top-cells
d_top <- q("
  SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY anom DESC) AS rank, cruise_key, dataset_key, site_key, depth_bin, depth_m,
         CAST(datetime AS DATE) AS date, v, clim_mean, n_cruises, anom
  FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL AND cruise_key <> {CRUISE} ORDER BY anom DESC LIMIT 15")
d_top |>
  transmute(
    `rank without 2026` = rank, cruise = cruise_key, series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"),
    station = site_key, `depth (m)` = glue("{depth_bin}–{depth_bin + 10}"), date,
    `observed (°C)` = round(v, 2), `normal (°C)` = round(clim_mean, 2), `baseline cruises` = n_cruises, `departure (°C)` = round(anom, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "The largest single departures in the record outside the fall 2026 cruise.")
```

```{r}
#| label: bad-cells
#| include: false
# two of those are not warm water: show it from the data rather than assert it
c94 <- q("SELECT depth_bin, v FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = '1994-01-31JD' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND site_key = '093.3 028.0' AND depth_bin >= 490 ORDER BY depth_bin")
c59 <- q("SELECT depth_m, v FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = '1959-10-31OR' AND site_key = '093.3 035.0' AND depth_m BETWEEN 30 AND 430 ORDER BY depth_m")
s59 <- diff(c59$v) / diff(c59$depth_m)
stopifnot(sd(s59) < 2e-3, nrow(c94) >= 2)          # a straight line: one slope from 30 m to 430 m
pre93 <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, anom, CAST(datetime AS DATE) AS date FROM cell
  WHERE anom IS NOT NULL AND cruise_year < 1993 AND NOT (cruise_key = '1959-10-31OR' AND site_key = '093.3 035.0')
  ORDER BY anom DESC LIMIT 1")
```

Among the `r fk(d_share$n_cells)` values with a normal, **the `r d_share$of_top_50` largest departures all belong to
the fall 2026 cruise**, and `r d_share$of_top_100` of the largest 100. `r d_share$n_above_prev` of its values exceed
the previous record of `r fs(k$prev_anom, 2)` °C.

Two entries in the table are bad data, not warm water, which is the weakness of ranking single values. The January
1994 value is `r f1(tail(c94$v, 1), 2)` °C in the last bin of a cast that reads `r f1(c94$v[nrow(c94) - 1], 2)` °C
ten metres above it. The October 1959 cast at station 93.3 35.0 falls in a perfectly straight line from
`r f1(c59$v[1], 1)` °C at `r round(c59$depth_m[1])` m to `r f1(tail(c59$v, 1), 1)` °C at `r round(tail(c59$depth_m, 1))` m
(`r f1(abs(mean(s59)) * 25, 2)` °C every 25 m):
values interpolated across a gap in the source, not measurements. Neither is flagged in the source data. Without
them the largest departure before 1993 is `r fs(pre93$anom, 2)` °C (`r format(pre93$date, "%B %Y")`).

### Layer averages over the same stations

The fairer comparison averages each cruise over one fixed set of stations, the ones the fall 2026 cruise occupied.
A station's departure profile is averaged over the layer's 10 m bins (bottle profiles are first interpolated in
depth onto those bins), then the stations are averaged. A cruise is ranked when it occupied at least 60 % of those
stations in a month that has a normal.

```{r}
#| label: fig-layers
#| fig-cap: "Every CalCOFI cruise since 1950 as one point: its mean temperature departure over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied, for the upper 50 m and for 50–200 m. Open circles are bottle casts, filled circles CTD. Bands mark the earlier warm events; the 1982–83 cruises occupied too few of these stations to be plotted and are in the table of events below. Preliminary data for 2026."
#| fig-alt: "Two time series of cruise-mean temperature departure from 1950 to 2026. Values mostly lie between minus 1 and plus 2 degrees Celsius. November 2015 reaches 3.4 in the upper 50 metres and February 1998 reaches 1.9 at 50 to 200 metres. Fall 2026 stands alone at 5.1 and 2.7."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.4
d_l <- d_layer |>
  filter(layer %in% c("0-50 m", "50-200 m")) |>
  mutate(date = date_min + (date_max - date_min) / 2, layer = factor(layer, c("0-50 m", "50-200 m"), c("0–50 m", "50–200 m")))
d_ev <- tibble(
  event = c("1957–59", "1982–83", "1997–98", "2014–16"),
  x0    = as.Date(c("1957-04-01", "1982-07-01", "1997-05-01", "2014-01-01")),
  x1    = as.Date(c("1959-12-31", "1983-12-31", "1998-08-31", "2016-06-30")))
l_top <- d_l |> filter(cruise_key == CRUISE)
l_run <- d_l |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> group_by(layer) |> slice_max(anom, n = 1, with_ties = F) |> ungroup()

ggplot(d_l, aes(date, anom)) +
  geom_rect(data = d_ev, aes(xmin = x0, xmax = x1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = F, fill = SAND) +
  geom_text(
    data = mutate(d_ev, layer = factor("0–50 m", levels(d_l$layer))), aes(x = x0 + (x1 - x0) / 2, y = 5.75, label = event),
    inherit.aes = F, colour = MUTED, size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = series, colour = series), size = 1.8, stroke = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = l_top, colour = COL_2026, size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(data = l_top, aes(label = glue("fall 2026  {fs(anom)} °C")), colour = INK, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -500) +
  geom_text(data = l_run, aes(label = glue("{format(date, '%b %Y')}  {fs(anom)}")), colour = INK, size = 3.1, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -400, nudge_y = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~ layer, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(bottle = 1, CTD = 16)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(bottle = INK, CTD = COL_NORM)) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(seq(1950, 2020, 10), "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fsa) +
  labs(
    title    = "Every CalCOFI cruise since 1950, averaged over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied",
    subtitle = "Mean temperature departure (°C) from the 1993–2013 normal of the cruise's month. Open: bottle casts. Filled: CTD.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = glue("CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). 2026 is preliminary.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(12, "pt"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-layer-rank
d_layer |>
  filter(layer != "0-200 m") |>
  group_by(layer, series) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(desc(anom)), `of cruises` = n()) |>
  filter(rank <= 6) |> ungroup() |>
  arrange(match(layer, c("surface (0-10 m)", "0-50 m", "50-200 m")), desc(series), rank) |>
  transmute(
    layer, series, rank, `of cruises`, cruise = cruise_key, stations = n_sta, `departure (°C)` = round(anom, 2),
    `warmest station (°C)` = round(anom_max_station, 2), `layer temperature (°C)` = round(temp, 2)) |>
  dt_(caption = "Cruises ranked by layer-mean departure over the fall 2026 stations, by series.")
```

```{r}
#| label: layer-numbers
#| include: false
both <- d_layer |> filter(layer == "0-50 m") |> select(cruise_key, series, anom) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = anom) |> filter(!is.na(bottle), !is.na(CTD))
n_ctd <- sum(d_layer$layer == "0-50 m" & d_layer$series == "CTD")
n_btl <- sum(d_layer$layer == "0-50 m" & d_layer$series == "bottle")
```

- **Upper 50 m: `r fs(k$l50, 2)` °C**, first of `r n_ctd` CTD cruises. The previous high is `r fs(k$l50_prev$anom, 2)` °C
  (`r k$l50_prev$cruise_key`); the bottle series, `r n_btl` cruises back to 1950, has nothing higher.
- **50–200 m: `r fs(k$l200, 2)` °C**, first. The previous high is `r fs(k$l200_prev$anom, 2)` °C
  (`r k$l200_prev$cruise_key`, the 1997–98 El Niño). The lead is narrower at depth.
- The two series agree where they overlap. Over the `r nrow(both)` cruises both cover, their upper-50 m means differ
  by `r f1(mean(abs(both$CTD - both$bottle)), 2)` °C on average and never by more than
  `r f1(max(abs(both$CTD - both$bottle)), 2)` °C, so the bottle series stands in fairly for the years before 1993.

### The earlier warm events

```{r}
#| label: tbl-events
d_events <- q("
  WITH ev AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('1957–59', 1957, 1959), ('1982–83 (through 1984)', 1982, 1984), ('1997–98', 1997, 1998),
                                    ('2014–16', 2014, 2016), ('2026', 2026, 2026)) t(event, y0, y1)),
  x AS (SELECT ev.event, l.* FROM cruise_layer l JOIN ev ON l.year BETWEEN ev.y0 AND ev.y1 WHERE l.layer IN ('0-50 m', '50-200 m')),
  m AS (SELECT event, layer, arg_max(cruise_key, anom) AS cruise_m, arg_max(n_sta, anom) AS n_m, max(anom) AS anom_m FROM x WHERE n_sta >= 7 GROUP BY ALL),
  s AS (SELECT event, layer, arg_max(cruise_key, anom_season) AS cruise_s, arg_max(n_sta_season, anom_season) AS n_s, max(anom_season) AS anom_s FROM x WHERE n_sta_season >= 7 GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT * FROM m FULL JOIN s USING (event, layer) ORDER BY layer, event")
d_events |>
  transmute(
    layer, event, `warmest cruise (monthly normal)` = cruise_m, stations = n_m, `departure (°C)` = round(anom_m, 2),
    `warmest cruise (seasonal normal)` = cruise_s, `stations ` = n_s, `departure from the seasonal normal (°C)` = round(anom_s, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Each warm event's warmest cruise over the fall 2026 stations (at least 7 of them occupied).")
```

The seasonal normal also reaches months that have no monthly normal, such as September and December 1997. The
1982–83 cruises occupied only 7 or 8 of these stations, so the next table compares them, and every other cruise,
on exactly the stations they share with fall 2026.

### On the stations two cruises share

```{r}
#| label: tbl-paired
d_pair_tbl <- q("
  WITH y AS (
    SELECT layer, 'departure from the monthly normal' AS yardstick, cruise_key, n_month AS n, anom_other AS other, anom_2026 AS y26 FROM paired WHERE n_month >= 10
    UNION ALL SELECT layer, 'departure from the seasonal normal', cruise_key, n_season, season_other, season_2026 FROM paired WHERE n_season >= 10
    UNION ALL SELECT layer, 'temperature itself (no baseline)', cruise_key, n_temp, temp_other, temp_2026 FROM paired WHERE n_temp >= 10)
  SELECT layer, yardstick, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises_compared, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE other >= y26) AS at_or_above_2026,
         arg_min(cruise_key, y26 - other) AS closest_cruise, arg_min(n, y26 - other) AS shared_stations,
         arg_min(other, y26 - other) AS closest_value, arg_min(y26, y26 - other) AS fall_2026, min(y26 - other) AS margin
  FROM y WHERE layer <> '0-200 m' GROUP BY layer, yardstick
  ORDER BY CASE layer WHEN 'surface (0-10 m)' THEN 0 WHEN '0-50 m' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, yardstick")
d_pair_tbl |>
  transmute(
    layer, yardstick, `cruises compared` = cruises_compared, `at or above fall 2026` = at_or_above_2026,
    `closest cruise` = closest_cruise, `shared stations` = shared_stations, `its value (°C)` = round(closest_value, 2),
    `fall 2026, same stations (°C)` = round(fall_2026, 2), `margin (°C)` = round(margin, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Fall 2026 against every other cruise on the stations both occupied (at least 10).")
```

```{r}
#| label: paired-numbers
#| include: false
pm    <- function(layer_, y_) d_pair_tbl |> filter(layer == layer_, grepl(y_, yardstick))
tie84 <- q("SELECT * FROM paired WHERE cruise_key = '1984-02-32NM' AND layer = '50-200 m'")
stopifnot(sum(d_pair_tbl$at_or_above_2026) == 0)
```

No cruise in the record equals fall 2026 on shared stations, in any layer, by any of the three yardsticks. The
third needs no baseline: it compares the layer's temperature itself, whatever the month. The margin is about
`r f1(pm("0-50 m", "monthly")$margin, 0)` °C in the upper 50 m and `r f1(pm("50-200 m", "itself")$margin)`–`r f1(pm("50-200 m", "monthly")$margin)` °C
at 50–200 m. With fewer shared stations the upper 50 m still holds; at depth it gets close: on the
`r tie84$n_month` offshore stations it shares with the February 1984 cruise, 50–200 m is a tie
(`r f1(tie84$anom_other, 2)` against `r f1(tie84$anom_2026, 2)` °C).

### Without any baseline

```{r}
#| label: fig-warmest
#| fig-cap: "The warmest water CalCOFI has measured in each 10 m depth bin on its core grid (lines 76.7–93.3, stations out to 120), in any month: before fall 2026 (grey) and on the fall 2026 cruise (red). Preliminary data for 2026."
#| fig-alt: "Two profiles of record temperature against depth. The 2026 profile is warmer than the previous record at every depth from the surface to 130 metres, by up to 3.8 degrees Celsius near 45 metres."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.8
d_warm <- q("
  WITH r AS (SELECT * FROM cell WHERE line BETWEEN 76.7 AND 93.4 AND station <= 120 AND depth_bin < 200 AND v < 35)
  SELECT depth_bin, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises,
         max(v) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE})  AS t_2026,
         max(v) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS t_before,
         arg_max(cruise_key, v) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS cruise_before,
         arg_max(site_key, v)   FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS station_before
  FROM r GROUP BY depth_bin ORDER BY depth_bin") |>
  mutate(depth_m = depth_bin + 5, margin = t_2026 - t_before)
z_rec   <- d_warm |> filter(margin > 0) |> pull(depth_bin)
warm_nc <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n, min(cruise_year) AS y0 FROM cell WHERE line BETWEEN 76.7 AND 93.4 AND station <= 120")
stopifnot(all(diff(z_rec) == 10), min(z_rec) == 0)   # one unbroken span from the surface down
w_big   <- d_warm |> slice_max(margin, n = 1)

ggplot(d_warm, aes(y = depth_m)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = \(d) filter(d, margin > 0), aes(xmin = t_before, xmax = t_2026), fill = COL_2026, alpha = 0.12, orientation = "y") +
  geom_path(aes(x = t_before), colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = t_before), colour = MUTED, size = 1.4) +
  geom_path(aes(x = t_2026), colour = COL_2026, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = t_2026), colour = COL_2026, size = 1.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 25.4, y = 68, label = "fall 2026", colour = INK, size = 3.4, hjust = 1, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 20.2, y = 24, label = "the warmest before,\nany cruise since 1949", colour = INK, size = 3.2, hjust = 1, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(0, 200, 25), expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", breaks = seq(10, 26, 4)) +
  labs(
    title    = glue("The warmest water on record at every depth from the surface to {max(z_rec) + 10} m"),
    subtitle = glue("Highest temperature (°C) in each 10 m bin, {warm_nc$n} cruises on the core grid, any month"),
    x = NULL, y = "Depth (m)") +
  theme_story()
```

On the core grid (`r warm_nc$n` cruises since `r warm_nc$y0`), every depth from the surface to `r max(z_rec) + 10` m
now has its record on the fall 2026 cruise: by `r f1(d_warm$margin[d_warm$depth_bin == 0])` °C at the surface
(the earlier record, `r f1(d_warm$t_before[d_warm$depth_bin == 0], 2)` °C, was set in
`r format(as.Date(paste0(substr(d_warm$cruise_before[d_warm$depth_bin == 0], 1, 7), "-01")), "%B %Y")`, a summer cruise) and by up to
`r f1(w_big$margin)` °C at `r w_big$depth_bin`–`r w_big$depth_bin + 10` m. Below `r max(z_rec) + 10` m, earlier
cruises were warmer.

### Every station ever occupied {#sec-whole-record}

The release's normal exists only where the cruises of 1993–2013 went: the stations of today's grid. CalCOFI also
worked lines far to the south, off Baja California, until the 1980s. None of the rankings above sees them, nor any
month that has no normal. One yardstick does: each value against the mean of the *other* cruises, before fall 2026,
of the same series at the same station, calendar month and depth bin, wherever at least five exist. It is a cruder
normal than the release's. Its years differ from station to station, and at today's stations it includes the warm
years since 2014, which makes recent departures read smaller.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-whole-record
# every value against the mean of the OTHER cruises, before fall 2026, of the same series at the same station,
# calendar month and 10 m bin (at least five of them, whatever their years)
invisible(dbExecute(con, glue_sql("
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE cell_others AS
  WITH g AS (
    SELECT dataset_key, site_key, cruise_month, depth_bin, count(*) AS n0, sum(v) AS s0
    FROM cell_ok WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT c.dataset_key, c.cruise_key, c.cruise_year, c.cruise_month, c.site_key, c.line, c.station, c.depth_bin, c.latitude, c.v, c.anom,
         CASE WHEN c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} THEN g.n0 ELSE g.n0 - 1 END AS n_others,
         CASE WHEN c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} THEN g.s0 / g.n0 ELSE (g.s0 - c.v) / (g.n0 - 1) END AS mean_others
  FROM cell_ok c JOIN g USING (dataset_key, site_key, cruise_month, depth_bin)
  WHERE CASE WHEN c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} THEN g.n0 ELSE g.n0 - 1 END >= 5", .con = con)))
wr <- q("
  SELECT count(*) AS cells, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises, count(*) FILTER (WHERE anom IS NULL) AS cells_no_normal,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE line >= 96) AS cells_south, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE line >= 96) AS cruises_south,
         max(v - mean_others) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS max_else,
         max(v - mean_others) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE})  AS max_2026
  FROM cell_others")
wr_all <- q("SELECT count(*) AS cells, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises, max(cruise_year) AS y1, count(anom) AS with_normal FROM cell WHERE line >= 96")   # line 96.7 and beyond
stopifnot(wr_all$with_normal == 0)
wr$n_above <- q("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND v - mean_others > {wr$max_else}")$n
d_wr <- q("
  (SELECT * FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE}  ORDER BY v - mean_others DESC LIMIT 3)
  UNION ALL
  (SELECT * FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} ORDER BY v - mean_others DESC LIMIT 12)") |>
  mutate(dep = v - mean_others) |> arrange(cruise_key != CRUISE, desc(dep))
w65 <- d_wr |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice(1)
w58 <- d_wr |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice(2)
stopifnot(w65$cruise_key == "1965-07-31AX", w58$cruise_key == "1958-10-31PT", wr$max_2026 > wr$max_else)
d_wr |>
  transmute(
    cruise = nb(cruise_key), series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"), station = sta(site_key),
    `latitude (°N)` = round(latitude, 1), `depth (m)` = nb(glue("{depth_bin}–{depth_bin + 10}")), `observed (°C)` = round(v, 2),
    `mean of the other cruises (°C)` = round(mean_others, 2), `other cruises` = n_others, `departure (°C)` = round(dep, 2),
    `has a 1993–2013 normal` = if_else(is.na(anom), "no", "yes")) |>
  kable(caption = "Departures from the mean of the other cruises at the same station, calendar month and depth: the three largest of fall 2026, then the twelve largest of every other cruise since 1950.")
```

Line 96.7 and the lines south of it hold `r fk(wr_all$cells)` values from `r wr_all$cruises` cruises (the last in
`r wr_all$y1`), none with a normal, and this yardstick reaches `r fk(wr$cells_south)` of them. In all it covers
`r fk(wr$cells)` values from `r wr$cruises` cruises, `r fk(wr$cells_no_normal)` of which have no 1993–2013 normal.

By this yardstick too the largest departures in the record are fall 2026's: `r fs(wr$max_2026)` °C at the most, with
`r wr$n_above` of its values above everything else. The largest earlier ones are on the southern lines:
`r fs(w65$dep)` °C at `r w65$depth_bin`–`r w65$depth_bin + 10` m at station `r sta(w65$site_key)`, off Baja California
at `r f1(w65$latitude)`°N, in July 1965, and `r fs(w58$dep)` °C at
`r w58$depth_bin`–`r w58$depth_bin + 10` m at station `r sta(w58$site_key)` (`r f1(w58$latitude)`°N) in October 1958,
during the 1957–59 El Niño. The second has the shape of fall 2026 at a smaller size: surface-layer water of
`r f1(w58$v)` °C at a depth where that station averages `r f1(w58$mean_others)` °C. The same waters gave the largest
value [published](#sec-literature) for the next great El Niño.

## Trends {#sec-trends}

### Every November cruise

```{r}
#| label: fig-novembers
#| fig-cap: "Sea-surface (0–10 m) temperature departure at each station on every November cruise with a CTD, 1998 to 2026. Each cruise is compared with the same 1993–2013 November normal; the number is the cruise's mean over its stations. There was no November cruise in 2018 or 2020 (the fall cruise sailed in October), nor in the years missing before 2014. A station with no normal is not drawn. Preliminary data from 2021."
#| fig-alt: "Twenty small maps, one per November cruise. Most are pale; 2014 and 2015 are light red; 2026 is red inshore, with fewer stations."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9.2
d_nov <- q("
  SELECT c.cruise_key, r.year, c.site_key, c.latitude AS lat, c.longitude AS lon, c.v, c.anom
  FROM cell c JOIN cruise_ref r USING (cruise_key)
  WHERE c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND c.cruise_month = 11 AND c.depth_bin = 0 AND c.anom IS NOT NULL")
d_novm <- d_nov |> group_by(cruise_key, year) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(anom), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(label = glue("{year}   {fs(mean)} °C   ({n} stations)"))
d_nov <- d_nov |> left_join(select(d_novm, cruise_key, label), by = "cruise_key") |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, d_novm$label[order(d_novm$year)]))
SFC_MAX <- ceiling(max(abs(d_nov$anom)))

ggplot(d_nov) +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = SAND, colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_point(aes(lon, lat, fill = anom), shape = 21, size = 1.9, colour = MUTED, stroke = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = cmocean("balance")(256), limits = c(-SFC_MAX, SFC_MAX), breaks = seq(-8, 8, 4), labels = fsa,
    name = "°C from the November normal",
    guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top", barwidth = unit(170, "pt"), barheight = unit(8, "pt"), frame.colour = STONE)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-124.9, -116.6), ylim = c(29.6, 35.3), expand = F) +
  labs(
    title    = "Twenty Novembers at the sea surface",
    subtitle = "Temperature departure (°C) at each station, 0–10 m. One colour scale for every year.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = glue("CalCOFI CTD; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary from 2021.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story(10) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#eaf1f6", colour = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8.2), legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = MUTED),
    panel.spacing = unit(6, "pt"))
```

The years after the baseline do not warm steadily. The surface was warm in 2014 and 2015
(`r fs(d_novm$mean[d_novm$year == 2014])` and `r fs(d_novm$mean[d_novm$year == 2015])` °C), near normal in 2021 and
2022, below normal in 2024 (`r fs(d_novm$mean[d_novm$year == 2024])` °C), and then `r fs(d_novm$mean[d_novm$year == 2026])` °C
in 2026, on a cruise that covered only the southern lines.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-novembers
# each November cruise at the surface: over its own stations, and over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied
d_novt <- q("
  WITH own AS (
    SELECT cruise_key, count(*) AS n_surface, count(anom) AS n_normal, avg(anom) AS anom_own
    FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND cruise_month = 11 AND depth_bin = 0 GROUP BY cruise_key)
  SELECT r.year, o.cruise_key, r.ship_name, r.ctd_stage, o.n_surface, o.n_normal, o.anom_own, l.n_sta AS n_2026, l.anom AS anom_2026
  FROM own o JOIN cruise_ref r USING (cruise_key)
  LEFT JOIN cruise_layer l ON l.cruise_key = o.cruise_key AND l.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND l.layer = 'surface (0-10 m)'
  ORDER BY r.year")
nov15 <- d_novt |> filter(year == 2015)
stopifnot(nov15$anom_2026 == max(d_novt$anom_2026[d_novt$year < 2026]))
d_novt |>
  transmute(
    year, cruise = nb(cruise_key), ship = str_to_title(ship_name), `stations with a surface value` = n_surface, `with a normal` = n_normal,
    `mean over its own stations (°C)` = round(anom_own, 2), `of the fall 2026 stations` = n_2026,
    `mean over those (°C)` = round(anom_2026, 2), `data stage` = ctd_stage) |>
  kable(caption = "Every November cruise at the sea surface (0–10 m): its mean departure over its own stations, and over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied.")
```

A cruise's own stations change from year to year, so the last columns put every November on the stations of the
fall 2026 cruise; these are the bars along the bottom of the [animation](#sec-video). On that footing the previous
high is `r fs(nov15$anom_2026)` °C in 2015 (`r nov15$n_2026` of the `r nrow(sfc)` stations), against
`r fs(d_novt$anom_2026[d_novt$year == 2026])` °C in 2026.

### Through 2026

```{r}
#| label: tbl-2026
d_26 <- q("
  SELECT l.cruise_key, c.date_min, c.date_max, l.layer, l.anom, l.n_sta
  FROM cruise_layer l JOIN cruise_ref c USING (cruise_key)
  WHERE l.year = 2026 AND l.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND l.layer IN ('surface (0-10 m)', '0-50 m', '50-200 m')") |>
  mutate(anom = round(anom, 2)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = c(anom, n_sta)) |>
  arrange(date_min)
d_26 |>
  transmute(
    cruise = cruise_key, dates = glue("{trimws(format(date_min, '%e %b'))} – {trimws(format(date_max, '%e %b'))}"),
    `surface (°C)` = `anom_surface (0-10 m)`, `0–50 m (°C)` = `anom_0-50 m`, `50–200 m (°C)` = `anom_50-200 m`,
    `stations (0–50 m)` = `n_sta_0-50 m`) |>
  kable(caption = "The four cruises of 2026: mean departure over the stations the fall cruise occupied, each against its own month's normal.")
```

The same stations were already about 2 °C warm in the upper 50 m in January and April 2026 and 1.5 °C warm in
July, with little signal below 50 m. Between July and November the upper 50 m gained a further
`r f1(d_26[["anom_0-50 m"]][4] - d_26[["anom_0-50 m"]][3])` °C of departure and the layer beneath it
`r f1(d_26[["anom_50-200 m"]][4] - d_26[["anom_50-200 m"]][3])` °C. The [buoy records](#fig-buoys) say the inshore
surface had been at 22 to 25 °C since at least late September.

### The long record

```{r}
#| label: trend
d_tr <- d_layer |>
  filter(layer == "0-50 m", cruise_key != CRUISE) |>
  mutate(t = as.numeric(date_min + (date_max - date_min) / 2 - as.Date("1990-01-01")) / 3652.5)   # decades from 1990
fit_b <- lm(anom ~ t, data = filter(d_tr, series == "bottle"))
fit_c <- lm(anom ~ t, data = filter(d_tr, series == "CTD"))
tr <- list(
  b = coef(summary(fit_b))["t", ], c = coef(summary(fit_c))["t", ],
  sd_b = sd(resid(fit_b)), sd_all = sd(d_tr$anom),
  yrs_b = range(filter(d_tr, series == "bottle")$year), yrs_c = range(filter(d_tr, series == "CTD")$year))
```

Over these stations the upper 50 m has warmed slowly: a straight-line fit to the bottle series
(`r tr$yrs_b[1]`–`r tr$yrs_b[2]`, `r nrow(fit_b$model)` cruises) rises by **`r f1(tr$b["Estimate"], 2)` °C per decade**
(standard error `r f1(tr$b["Std. Error"], 2)`), and the CTD series (`r tr$yrs_c[1]`–`r tr$yrs_c[2]`, without the fall
2026 cruise) by `r f1(tr$c["Estimate"], 2)` °C per decade (standard error `r f1(tr$c["Std. Error"], 2)`). Cruises are
unevenly spaced and successive cruises are not independent, so these standard errors are too small; the slopes are a
description, not a test.

The fall 2026 departure is not a point on that line. Cruise-to-cruise scatter over the whole record has a standard
deviation of `r f1(tr$sd_all, 2)` °C, so `r fs(k$l50)` °C is `r f1(k$l50 / tr$sd_all, 0)` standard deviations from
normal, and `r f1(k$l50 - k$l50_prev$anom)` °C beyond anything else in it.

## The water mass {#sec-watermass}

```{r}
#| label: fig-ts
#| fig-cap: "Temperature against salinity for every one-metre value of the fall 2026 down casts in the upper 200 m: stations of the inner Southern California Bight (red) and stations seaward of them (blue). The black line is the 1993–2013 November normal at station 93.3 30.0 from the bottle series, with its depths marked. Grey curves are lines of equal density (sigma-theta, kg m⁻³). Preliminary data."
#| fig-alt: "A temperature-salinity diagram. The offshore casts and the normal curve lie at salinities of 33.0 to 33.7. The inshore casts extend to 25 degrees Celsius and salinity 34.4 to 34.5, far from any normal value."
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
d_ts <- q("
  SELECT t.site_key, t.depth_m, t.value AS temp, s.value AS sal
  FROM cast_1m t JOIN cast_1m s USING (sample_key, depth_m)
  WHERE t.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND s.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr'
    AND t.direction = 'd' AND t.measurement_qual IS NULL AND s.measurement_qual IS NULL AND t.depth_m <= 200") |>
  mutate(group = if_else(site_key %in% inner$site_key, "inner Bight", "seaward"))
# the normal curve is the BOTTLE series' (temperature and salinity at the bottle depths): the CTD salinity normal at
# this station is inflated at 90-120 m by one unflagged cast (see the note under the figure)
d_tsn <- q("
  SELECT t.depth_bin, t.clim_mean AS temp, s.clim_mean AS sal
  FROM climatology t JOIN climatology s USING (dataset_key, site_key, month, depth_bin)
  WHERE t.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.measurement_type = 'salinity' AND t.dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'
    AND t.site_key = {k$top_site} AND t.month = 11 AND t.depth_bin <= 200 AND t.clim_mean IS NOT NULL AND s.clim_mean IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY t.depth_bin")
d_bad <- q("
  SELECT c.depth_bin, c.clim_mean AS ctd_normal, c.clim_sd, b.clim_mean AS bottle_normal,
         (SELECT max(value) FROM obs_env o WHERE o.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND o.site_key = c.site_key
            AND o.cruise_key = '2007-11-32NM' AND o.depth_bin = c.depth_bin) AS cast_2007
  FROM climatology c LEFT JOIN climatology b
    ON b.measurement_type = 'salinity' AND b.dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle' AND b.site_key = c.site_key AND b.month = c.month AND b.depth_bin = c.depth_bin
  WHERE c.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND c.site_key = {k$top_site} AND c.month = 11
    AND c.depth_bin BETWEEN 90 AND 120 ORDER BY c.depth_bin")
# lines of equal density (TEOS-10, at the sea surface)
d_sig <- expand_grid(sal = seq(32.7, 34.8, 0.02), temp = seq(8, 26.5, 0.1)) |>
  mutate(sigma = gsw_sigma0(gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, 0, -118, 33), gsw_CT_from_t(gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, 0, -118, 33), temp, 0)))
d_sig_lab <- d_sig |> filter(abs(temp - 26.2) < 0.01) |> mutate(s_ = round(sigma * 2) / 2) |>
  filter(s_ %in% c(22, 23), abs(sigma - s_) < 0.008) |> group_by(s_) |> slice(1)

ggplot(d_ts, aes(sal, temp)) +
  geom_contour(data = d_sig, aes(z = sigma), breaks = seq(21, 27, 0.5), colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(data = d_sig_lab, aes(label = s_), colour = MUTED, size = 2.8, vjust = -0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_path(data = d_tsn, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = filter(d_tsn, depth_bin %in% c(0, 50, 100, 200)), colour = INK, size = 1.9) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(d_tsn, depth_bin %in% c(0, 50, 100, 200)), aes(label = glue("{depth_bin} m")), colour = INK, size = 2.9,
    bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.18, nudge_x = -0.07, direction = "y", segment.colour = NA, seed = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 34.44, y = 24.45, label = "inner Bight,\nsurface to 55 m", colour = INK, size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0, vjust = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 33.05, y = 21.2, label = "seaward stations", colour = INK, size = 3.1, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 34.14, y = 13.6, label = "November normal,\nstation 93.3 30.0\n(bottle series)", colour = INK, size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("inner Bight" = COL_2026, seaward = COL_NORM)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(33, 34.5, 0.5), limits = c(32.85, 34.72), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 26, 4), limits = c(8, 26.6), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "The warm layer is saltier than anything normally found here",
    subtitle = "Temperature (°C) against salinity, fall 2026 down casts, surface to 200 m",
    x = "Salinity", y = NULL) +
  theme_story()
```

```{r}
#| label: watermass-numbers
#| include: false
RHO_CP <- 1025 * 3990                       # J m-3 K-1: sea water's density times its specific heat
hc <- d_sta |> filter(layer == "0-200 m", !is.na(anom)) |> mutate(gj = anom * 200 * RHO_CP / 1e9)
hc_top <- hc |> slice_max(gj, n = 1)
wm <- list(
  s_inner = d_ts |> filter(group == "inner Bight", depth_m <= 40) |> pull(sal) |> quantile(c(0.1, 0.9)),
  s_outer = d_ts |> filter(group == "seaward",     depth_m <= 40) |> pull(sal) |> quantile(c(0.1, 0.9)),
  s_norm  = range(d_tsn$sal[d_tsn$depth_bin <= 40]), s_norm_max = max(d_tsn$sal),
  days    = hc_top$gj * 1e9 / (100 * 86400))
stopifnot(nrow(d_tsn) >= 8, !anyNA(d_bad$bottle_normal[d_bad$depth_bin >= 100]), k$sal[1] > wm$s_norm_max)   # the layer at the two core stations is saltier than the whole normal column to 200 m
```

Temperature alone cannot say where water came from; temperature and salinity together can. The seaward stations
plot where the California Current always does: fresh at the surface (`r f1(wm$s_outer[1], 1)`–`r f1(wm$s_outer[2], 1)`
in the top 40 m) and saltier with depth. The normal profile at the record station does the same
(`r f1(wm$s_norm[1], 2)`–`r f1(wm$s_norm[2], 2)` in the top 40 m, `r f1(wm$s_norm_max, 2)` at 200 m). Across the inner
Bight the top 40 m is `r f1(wm$s_inner[1], 1)` to `r f1(wm$s_inner[2], 1)`, and at stations 28 and 30 the warm layer
(`r f1(k$sal[1], 2)`–`r f1(k$sal[2], 2)`) is saltier than any water the normal column holds down to 200 m, while
lying at the surface, where the normal is freshest. Local heating moves water straight up on this diagram; it cannot
move it to the right.

The quantity of heat makes the same point. Through the upper 200 m at station `r hc_top$site_key` the water column
holds about **`r f1(hc_top$gj)` GJ per square metre** more heat than normal
(`r f1(mean(hc$gj))` GJ m⁻² on average over the `r nrow(hc)` stations sampled to 200 m). At a net surface heating of
100 W m⁻², a generous figure chosen only for scale, the atmosphere would need about `r fk(round(wm$days, -1))` days to
supply it. Both the salt and the heat say this water was carried in, not warmed where it lies. The
[Scripps Pier record](#fig-pier) shows it arriving at the coast: salinity there rose by `r f1(p_pk$s26 - p_c0$s26, 1)`
within about ten days.

### Warm and salty, or only warm? {#sec-salt}

Salinity also separates this event from the last one. The table puts every cruise on one footing: its mean
departure through the upper 50 m at the stations of the inner Bight, in temperature and in salinity, against the
bottle series' normals. Earlier cruises are their bottle casts; fall 2026 is its CTD, whose salinity
[matches the bottles drawn on board](#tbl-bottles).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ts-events
ts59 <- d_tsx |> filter(year %in% 1957:1959) |> slice_max(t_anom, n = 1)
d_tsx |>
  mutate(s_rank = rank(-s_anom)) |>
  slice_max(t_anom, n = 8) |>
  transmute(
    cruise = nb(cruise_key), stations = n_s, `temperature (°C)` = round(t_anom, 2), `salinity` = round(s_anom, 2),
    `salinity, station by station` = glue("{fs(s_min, 2)} to {fs(s_max, 2)}"), `salinity rank` = s_rank) |>
  kable(caption = glue("The eight warmest cruises in the inner Southern California Bight, upper 50 m: mean departure of temperature and of salinity from the bottle series' normals, and where the salinity departure ranks among the {nrow(d_tsx)} cruises with at least 8 of these stations."))
```

The warm water of 2014–15 was warm only. November 2015 stands `r fs(tsx("2015-11-32OC")$t_anom)` °C above normal and
`r fs0(tsx("2015-11-32OC")$s_anom)` in salinity; the State of the California Current report of the time found the
upper ocean "unusually fresh during 2015 in most regions off southern California" [@mcclatchie2016]. The water of the
1997–98 El Niño was warm and salty: `r fs(tsx("1998-02-31JD")$t_anom)` °C and `r fs(tsx("1998-02-31JD")$s_anom, 2)` in
February 1998, when the inshore countercurrent carried "a salinity anomaly as much as +0.5" [@lynn1998]. The 1957–59
warm period has the same sign: about 0.2 in the mixed layer of January 1958 [@reid1960], and
`r fs(ts59$s_anom, 2)` here in `r month.name[ts59$cruise_month]` `r ts59$year`. The 1982–83 El Niño differed again:
its subsurface water was fresher than normal [@simpson1984a].

Fall 2026 is of the salty kind and beyond it: `r fs(ts26$s_anom, 2)`, the highest of the `r nrow(d_tsx)` cruises,
where the cruise-to-cruise standard deviation is `r f1(sd(d_tsx$s_anom[d_tsx$cruise_key != CRUISE]), 2)`. The seasonal
normal reaches more cruises (`r nrow(d_tss)`, September 1997 among them) and orders them the same way:
`r fs(d_tss$s_season[1], 2)` for fall 2026, `r fs(d_tss$s_season[2], 2)` for February 1998. By its salt
this water resembles what the 1997 El Niño brought to Baja California, 0.8 above normal on line 120 in October 1997
[@lynn1998], more than anything measured before off Southern California.

### Displaced water, or different water? {#sec-isopycnals}

A deep warm layer pushes everything beneath it down, and that alone makes large departures at a fixed depth: the
water at 100 m is warm partly because it is water that normally sits at 30 m. Following surfaces of equal density
separates the two effects: how far each surface moved, and whether the water on it changed. This is done here at
the record station from the one-metre down casts: fall 2026, and the casts of the `r nrow(b_in)` November cruises
behind its normal.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-isopycnals
# every one-metre down cast at the record station: the baseline's November cruises and fall 2026
d_iso <- q("
  WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full_base UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full)
  SELECT f.cruise_key, f.depth_min_m AS depth_m,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave')   AS temp,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr') AS sal
  FROM f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE s.site_key = {k$top_site} AND right(f.sample_key, 1) = 'd' AND f.measurement_qual IS NULL
    AND f.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr')
  GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY f.cruise_key, depth_m") |>
  filter(!is.na(temp), !is.na(sal)) |>
  mutate(
    sa    = gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, depth_m, top$longitude, top$latitude),
    sigma = gsw_sigma0(sa, gsw_CT_from_t(sa, temp, depth_m)),          # potential density anomaly, kg m-3 (TEOS-10)
    when  = if_else(cruise_key == CRUISE, "fall 2026", "normal"))

# depth, temperature and salinity where a cast first reaches each density (NA where the cast never holds it)
SIG <- seq(24.5, 26.5, 0.5)
on_sigma <- function(d, ...) {
  d <- arrange(d, depth_m) |> mutate(sig_m = cummax(sigma))            # a stable column: density never falls with depth
  tibble(sigma = SIG) |> mutate(
    depth = approx(d$sig_m, d$depth_m, xout = sigma, ties = min, rule = 1)$y,
    temp  = approx(d$depth_m, d$temp, xout = depth)$y,
    sal   = approx(d$depth_m, d$sal,  xout = depth)$y)}
d_on  <- d_iso |> group_by(cruise_key, when) |> group_modify(on_sigma) |> ungroup()
d_onn <- d_on |> filter(when == "normal") |> group_by(sigma) |>
  summarize(n = sum(!is.na(depth)), across(c(depth, temp, sal), list(mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = T), sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = T))), .groups = "drop")
d_on26 <- d_on |> filter(when == "fall 2026") |> select(sigma, depth_26 = depth, temp_26 = temp, sal_26 = sal)
d_surf <- left_join(d_onn, d_on26, by = "sigma") |> filter(n == nrow(b_in), !is.na(depth_26))

d_surf |>
  transmute(
    `density surface (σθ, kg m⁻³)` = f1(sigma),
    `normal depth (m)` = glue("{round(depth_mean)} ± {round(depth_sd)}"), `depth in 2026 (m)` = round(depth_26),
    `deeper by (m)` = round(depth_26 - depth_mean),
    `normal temperature (°C)` = glue("{f1(temp_mean, 2)} ± {f1(temp_sd, 2)}"), `in 2026 (°C)` = round(temp_26, 2),
    `warmer by (°C)` = round(temp_26 - temp_mean, 2),
    `normal salinity` = glue("{f1(sal_mean, 2)} ± {f1(sal_sd, 2)}"), `in 2026` = round(sal_26, 2), `saltier by` = round(sal_26 - sal_mean, 2)) |>
  kable(align = "r", caption = glue("Station 93.3 30.0 on surfaces of equal density: fall 2026 beside the mean (± 1 standard deviation) of the {nrow(b_in)} November baseline casts."))
```

```{r}
#| label: isopycnal-numbers
#| include: false
# the density of the sea surface (top 5 m) in each baseline cast, and the depth at which fall 2026 first reaches it
sig0   <- d_iso |> filter(when == "normal", depth_m <= 5) |> group_by(cruise_key) |> summarize(s = mean(sigma)) |> pull(s)
c26    <- d_iso |> filter(when == "fall 2026") |> arrange(depth_m) |> mutate(sig_m = cummax(sigma))
z_mean <- c26$depth_m[which(c26$sig_m >= mean(sig0))[1]]
z_min  <- c26$depth_m[which(c26$sig_m >= min(sig0))[1]]
iso <- list(
  sig0 = mean(sig0), sig0_min = min(sig0), z_mean = z_mean, z_min = z_min, sig26_0 = mean(c26$sigma[c26$depth_m <= 5]),
  dz = range(d_surf$depth_26 - d_surf$depth_mean), dt = range(d_surf$temp_26 - d_surf$temp_mean), ds = range(d_surf$sal_26 - d_surf$sal_mean),
  dt_sd = range((d_surf$temp_26 - d_surf$temp_mean) / d_surf$temp_sd))
# split the departure at 150 m into the part from displacement and the part from changed water
z_   <- 150
t26  <- approx(c26$depth_m, c26$temp, z_)$y
s26  <- approx(c26$depth_m, c26$sig_m, z_)$y
n_pr <- d_iso |> filter(when == "normal") |> group_by(depth_m) |> summarize(temp = mean(temp), sigma = mean(sigma), n = n()) |>
  filter(n == nrow(b_in)) |> arrange(depth_m) |> mutate(sig_m = cummax(sigma))
tn_z  <- approx(n_pr$depth_m, n_pr$temp, z_)$y                                   # the normal temperature at 150 m
z_n   <- approx(n_pr$sig_m, n_pr$depth_m, s26, ties = min)$y                     # where the normal column holds that density
tn_s  <- approx(n_pr$depth_m, n_pr$temp, z_n)$y                                  # and its temperature there
split <- list(z = z_, total = t26 - tn_z, heave = tn_s - tn_z, water = t26 - tn_s, z_n = z_n)
stopifnot(abs(split$total - split$heave - split$water) < 1e-9, iso$z_min > 60)
```

Two things stand out.

**The upper `r round(iso$z_min)` m is not normal water pushed down.** In the baseline casts the sea surface has a
density of `r f1(iso$sig0, 2)` kg m⁻³ on average, and `r f1(iso$sig0_min, 2)` in the lightest of them. In fall 2026
the surface was `r f1(iso$sig26_0, 2)`, and the water did not become as dense as the lightest baseline surface until
**`r round(iso$z_min)` m** (as dense as the average one until `r round(iso$z_mean)` m). Everything above that depth is
lighter than any water those six casts contain. It has no counterpart in the normal column to have been displaced
from: it is water that is not normally there.

**Beneath it, the density surfaces lay `r round(iso$dz[1])` to `r round(iso$dz[2])` m deeper than normal, and the
water on them had changed as well.** On the same surfaces it was `r f1(iso$dt[1])` to `r f1(iso$dt[2])` °C warmer and
`r f1(iso$ds[1], 2)` to `r f1(iso$ds[2], 2)` saltier than the baseline mean, `r f1(iso$dt_sd[1], 0)` to
`r f1(iso$dt_sd[2], 0)` standard deviations of the six casts. At `r split$z` m, for example, the departure of
`r fs(split$total)` °C splits into `r fs(split$heave)` °C from displacement (the water there has the density the
normal column holds at `r round(split$z_n)` m) and `r fs(split$water)` °C from the water itself being warmer on that
surface.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-isopycnals-cruise
# the same on every station of the cruise: the baseline is the median of the six cruises' down casts at the station
d_ia <- q("
  WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full_base UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full)
  SELECT f.cruise_key, s.site_key, f.depth_min_m AS depth_m,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave')   AS temp,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr') AS sal
  FROM f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE right(f.sample_key, 1) = 'd' AND f.measurement_qual IS NULL AND f.depth_min_m <= 450
    AND f.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr') AND s.site_key IN ({unique(d_sta$site_key)*})
  GROUP BY ALL") |>
  filter(!is.na(temp), !is.na(sal)) |>
  mutate(
    sa    = gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, depth_m, -119, 33),
    sigma = gsw_sigma0(sa, gsw_CT_from_t(sa, temp, depth_m)),
    when  = if_else(cruise_key == CRUISE, "fall 2026", "normal"))
SIG_ALL <- c(25.5, 26)
d_oa <- d_ia |> group_by(site_key, cruise_key, when) |>
  group_modify(\(d, ...) on_sigma(d) |> filter(sigma %in% SIG_ALL)) |> ungroup()
d_dz <- d_oa |> filter(when == "normal") |> group_by(site_key, sigma) |>
  summarize(n = sum(!is.na(depth)), depth_n = median(depth, na.rm = T), temp_n = median(temp, na.rm = T), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 4) |>
  inner_join(d_oa |> filter(when == "fall 2026", !is.na(depth)) |> select(site_key, sigma, depth_26 = depth, temp_26 = temp), by = c("site_key", "sigma")) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(site_key %in% inner$site_key, "inner Bight", "seaward"), dz = depth_26 - depth_n, dt = temp_26 - temp_n)
d_dz |>
  group_by(`density surface (σθ)` = f1(sigma), stations = group) |>
  summarize(
    `stations with a baseline` = n(), `median deeper by (m)` = round(median(dz)), `range (m)` = glue("{round(min(dz))} to {round(max(dz))}"),
    `median warmer on the surface (°C)` = round(median(dt), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(align = "r", caption = "Every station of the cruise deep enough to hold the surface: how far two density surfaces lay below their baseline depth (the median of the six November baseline casts at the station), and the temperature change on them.")
```

The displacement is not confined to the record station. Across the cruise the same surfaces lay deeper than their
baseline at `r sum(d_dz$dz > 0)` of `r nrow(d_dz)` station-surface pairs: by a median of
`r round(median(d_dz$dz[d_dz$group == "inner Bight"]))` m in the inner Bight and
`r round(median(d_dz$dz[d_dz$group == "seaward"]))` m at the seaward stations.

So the depressed pycnocline accounts for most of the departure below about `r round(iso$z_min)` m, as expected of a
deep warm layer, and the layer itself is a different water mass. A baseline on density surfaces for every station,
built from the one-metre casts of the whole baseline period, would make this routine; here it is done by hand, from
six cruises.

::: {.callout-note title="A flaw in the salinity normal, found while drawing this figure"}
The diagram draws the normal from the bottle series because the CTD salinity normal at this station is wrong at
`r min(d_bad$depth_bin)`–`r max(d_bad$depth_bin) + 10` m: `r f1(min(d_bad$ctd_normal), 2)`–`r f1(max(d_bad$ctd_normal), 2)`
where the bottles give `r f1(min(d_bad$bottle_normal, na.rm = T), 2)`–`r f1(max(d_bad$bottle_normal, na.rm = T), 2)`.
One cast of the November 2007 cruise carries unflagged salinities up to `r f1(max(d_bad$cast_2007, na.rm = T), 2)` there,
which no water off California reaches, and they enter the mean. It does not touch the temperature normal, nor the
salinity normal of the warm layer above 60 m, whose standard deviation is about `r f1(mean(d_sal$sd), 2)`. It is
recorded here because this analysis is where it surfaced.
:::

## The event in context {#sec-context}

### What the agencies were reporting in fall 2026

These are other institutions' statements, quoted as published and read on 12–13 November 2026. They are context
for the measurements above, not part of them.

- **A strong El Niño is in progress.** NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, in its
  [ENSO Diagnostic Discussion of 12 November 2026](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_disc_nov2026/ensodisc.shtml)
  [@cpc_ensodisc_2026_11], keeps an El Niño Advisory in force: "El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely
  through January-March 2027". Its Niño-3.4 index for October was +2.5 °C. That is a *relative* index (the tropical
  mean is subtracted [@vanoldenborgh2021; @lheureux2024]), which NOAA has used officially since February 2026, so it is not comparable with the
  Niño-3.4 values quoted for earlier events without saying which index is meant. At the equator NOAA reports "a
  deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean": large
  departures at thermocline depth are how this event looks at its source as well.
- **A marine heatwave was already there.** NOAA Fisheries'
  [California Current Marine Heatwave Tracker](https://www.integratedecosystemassessment.noaa.gov/regions/california-current/california-current-marine-heatwave-tracker-blobtracker)
  (updated 30 October 2026) [@noaa_blobtracker_2026] has followed a heatwave off California, NEP25A, since May 2025, and says of the
  recent warming: "Although the current MHW off California preceded the El Niño, we now infer that we are seeing
  additional warming due to El Niño, primarily through the arrival of Kelvin waves, which act to further deepen the
  surface mixed layer, reduce upwelling, and therefore lead to surface layer warming. It is unclear if we can
  separate the warming that was already in place in California from the additional warming due to the El
  Niño-forced Kelvin waves."
- **Scripps Pier's century-long record.** The Shore Stations Program has measured the sea surface at the pier by
  hand every day since 1916. Its [plot for 2026](https://shorestations.ucsd.edu/plots/SST_This_Year.png) [@shorestations_plots_2026] gives
  24.0 °C for 12 November, counts 74 daily record highs in 2026 so far, and marks the days of early November as
  records for their dates. (This is the long manual record; the [automated station above](#fig-pier) is a separate
  instrument on the same pier.)
- **Gliders.** Scripps's underwater gliders have repeated CalCOFI line 90 for twenty years. The group's
  [El Niño page](https://spraydata.ucsd.edu/products/el-nino/) [@spray_elnino_2026] says of that line: "The warm water anomaly is now
  extending the deepest we've seen in 20 years of monitoring."
- **A published anomaly at thermocline depth, farther north.** In Monterey Bay, MBARI
  [reported on 29 October 2026](https://www.mbari.org/news/mbari-researchers-observe-the-arrival-of-el-nino-in-monterey-bay/)
  [@mbari_2026] that the temperature at 60 m "reached 18.18 degrees Celsius (64.72 degrees Fahrenheit), surpassing the time series
  record high set on November 19, 1997", with temperatures "more than seven degrees centigrade over the long-term
  average". That is the same kind of number as the one on this page, a departure at the depth of the thermocline,
  from an independent mooring about 600 km to the north-west, and a little over half as large.

Read together: the water CalCOFI measured arrived on top of a marine heatwave that had been in place for a year
and a half, during a strong El Niño. The measurements on this page do not separate the two, and NOAA says it
cannot yet either.

### The glider index, not yet at its record in September

```{r}
#| label: fig-glider
#| fig-cap: "The Southern California Temperature Index of the Scripps glider group: the temperature departure at 50 m along CalCOFI line 90 from the coast to 200 km offshore, as a three-month running mean, monthly from January 2007 to the latest value published when this page was rendered. Data: California Underwater Glider Network, doi:10.21238/S8SPRAY7292."
#| fig-alt: "A time series from 2007 to 2026. The index stays within about 1.5 degrees of zero until 2014, peaks at 3.3 degrees in December 2015, and rises steeply through 2026 to 2.8 degrees in September."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.6
gl_last <- slice_tail(d_gl, n = 1)
gl_top  <- slice_max(d_gl, scti, n = 1)
gl_rank <- sum(d_gl$scti > gl_last$scti) + 1
# CalCOFI's own casts on that stretch of line 90, at 50-60 m: the cruises whose six stations all have a normal
d_l90 <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, count(*) AS n, avg(anom) AS anom, string_agg(CAST(CAST(station AS INTEGER) AS VARCHAR), ' ' ORDER BY station) AS stations
  FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND line = 90 AND station BETWEEN 27 AND 54 AND depth_bin = 50 AND anom IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY cruise_key")
l90 <- function(cruise) d_l90 |> filter(cruise_key == cruise)
stopifnot(l90(CRUISE)$stations == l90("2015-11-32OC")$stations, l90(CRUISE)$n == 6, gl_top$date > as.Date("2015-10-01"), gl_top$date < as.Date("2016-02-01"))

ggplot(d_gl, aes(date, scti)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = COL_NORM, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = gl_top, colour = COL_2015, size = 2.6) +
  geom_point(data = gl_last, colour = COL_2026, size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(data = gl_top, aes(label = glue("{format(date, '%b %Y')}  {fs(scti)} °C")), colour = INK, size = 3.3, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -200, nudge_y = 0.1) +
  geom_text(data = gl_last, aes(label = glue("{format(date, '%b %Y')}  {fs(scti)} °C")), colour = INK, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -200) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(seq(2008, 2026, 2), "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fsa) +
  labs(
    title    = "At 50 m on line 90, the gliders' three-month mean was climbing toward its 2015 record",
    subtitle = "Southern California Temperature Index (°C): coast to 200 km offshore, three-month running mean",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Scripps Instrument Development Group, California Underwater Glider Network (doi:10.21238/S8SPRAY7292).") +
  theme_story()
```

The glider group publishes one number for line 90, the Southern California Temperature Index (@fig-glider): "the interannual
temperature anomaly at 50m depth along the coastal section of Line 90 (coast to 200-km offshore) with a 3-month
running mean applied" [@rudnick2017data]. Its latest value, centred on `r format(gl_last$date, "%B %Y")`, is
`r fs(gl_last$scti)` °C, the `r c("highest", "second highest", "third highest")[gl_rank]` of `r nrow(d_gl)` months since
2007; the record is `r fs(gl_top$scti)` °C, centred on `r format(gl_top$date, "%B %Y")`. The index ends six weeks before
the cruise and averages three months, so it does not yet cover what the ship found, and it neither confirms nor
contradicts it. CalCOFI's own casts on that stretch of the line say what to expect: its six stations averaged
`r fs(l90(CRUISE)$anom)` °C at 50–60 m on the fall 2026 cruise, and `r fs(l90("2015-11-32OC")$anom)` °C in November
2015, when the index centred on that month was `r fs(d_gl$scti[d_gl$month == "2015-11"])` °C. The index for
November 2026 will be the independent check on a record at that depth.

### How large earlier warm events were {#sec-literature}

What their observers published about the earlier warm events, with the baseline each used. No study uses the
1993–2013 normal of this page, and most report averages over a cruise, a section or a month, not single stations,
so sizes compare only loosely. Words in quotation marks are the authors'.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-literature
# published values, each read in the source named (or in its abstract, where the last column says so)
d_lit <- read_csv(file.path(DIR_DATA, "literature_ranges.csv"))
d_lit |>
  transmute(
    event, `where and what` = what, reported, `against` = baseline,
    source = glue("[@{key}]{if_else(read == 'abstract', ' (abstract)', '')}")) |>
  kable(caption = "Temperature departures published for earlier warm events off Southern California and Baja California, each against its own baseline.")
```

```{r}
#| label: literature-numbers
#| include: false
e97   <- evm("1997–98")
e83   <- evm("1982–83")
n97   <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT site_key) AS n FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = {e97$cruise_s}")$n
a9060 <- q("SELECT max(anom_season) AS a FROM cell_ok WHERE cruise_key = {e97$cruise_s} AND site_key = '090.0 060.0'")$a
o9060 <- q("SELECT max(v - mean_others) AS a FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key = {e97$cruise_s} AND site_key = '090.0 060.0'")$a
n9711 <- q("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM cell WHERE datetime >= TIMESTAMP '1997-11-10' AND datetime < TIMESTAMP '1997-12-01'")$n
stopifnot(e97$cruise_s == "1997-12-32QU", n9711 == 0, a9060 > 5)
```

Three things follow from setting these beside the release.

**The ranking sees the earlier events at the sizes their observers reported.** The largest value in the table for
today's grid is the "greater than 6°" that @hayward1999 found in the thermocline at station 90.60 in December 1997.
That cruise is in the release (`r e97$cruise_s`, `r n97` stations). Its largest value here is `r fs(e97$anom_s)` °C, at
station `r sta(e97$site_s)`, `r e97$bin_s`–`r e97$bin_s + 10` m, against the seasonal normal because December has no
monthly one. At station 90.60 itself the release gives `r fs(a9060)` °C against that normal, which is not the
paper's 1950–92 baseline, and `r fs(o9060)` °C against the mean of the other December cruises. For 1982–83 the release's largest is `r fs(e83$anom)` °C
(`r e83$cruise_key`, station `r sta(e83$site_key)`, `r e83$depth_bin`–`r e83$depth_bin + 10` m), where @mclain1985 give
"+5° to +6°C at 100 m". For November 2015 the upper 50 m averages `r fs(k$l50_prev$anom)` °C over the fall 2026
stations, where glider sections gave departures "frequently greater than 3 °C" for 10–100 m against 2007–2013
[@ren2021]. One cruise the literature
describes is not in the release: NOAA ship *McArthur*, 17–22 November 1997, the first of the extra cruises added
that winter [@lynn1998], on which station 90.30 showed thermocline departures "greater than 4°" [@hayward1999].

**The largest published value is from Baja California, and it is smaller.** On the first cruise of the Mexican
IMECOCAL programme, in early October 1997, the water 30 to 40 m down off Punta Eugenia (line 120) was 8 °C above
the 1950–78 October mean and 0.8 saltier [@lynn1998], "up to 8.7 °C" at 50 m [@durazo2002]. That cruise is not in
the CalCOFI database. CalCOFI's own casts on those lines in the 1957–59 El Niño are, and the
[whole-record ranking](#sec-whole-record) finds the same size there, `r fs(w58$dep)` °C in October 1958. It is the
nearest published analogue to fall 2026: a warm, salty surface layer lying where the thermocline normally is, in
the autumn of a very strong El Niño. Fall 2026 found that structure off San Diego, and larger.

**At the sea surface fall 2026 is not beyond what 2014–16 produced; beneath it, it is.** The largest departures
published for 2014–16 near the surface off Southern California are about 6 °C: 6.2 °C in satellite sea-surface
temperature [@gentemann2017] and 5.8 °C in daily bottom temperature at 7–10 m in the Santa Barbara Channel
[@reed2016]. That is the size of the `r f1(min(inner$anom), 0)` to `r f1(max(inner$anom), 0)` °C at the inner-Bight
stations of this cruise. The difference is
underneath. In 2015 the warming was "confined to the surface layer (upper ~50 m)" [@leising2015] and reached 0.5 to
1.5 °C at 100 m [@mcclatchie2016]; in fall 2026 the 50–200 m layer averages `r fs(k$l200)` °C over `r k$l200_n`
stations. That is why the record on this page rests on the values below the surface and on the layer averages, not
on the sea surface.

### Marine heatwaves, and why the largest numbers are below the surface {#sec-mhw}

A marine heatwave has a standard definition: "a prolonged discrete anomalously warm water event" that "lasts for
five or more days, with temperatures warmer than the 90th percentile based on a 30-year historical baseline
period" [@hobday2016], graded from moderate to extreme by how many times the local gap between the mean and that
percentile is exceeded [@hobday2018]. It is defined on daily sea-surface temperature, which a cruise cannot supply.
NOAA's tracker identifies heatwaves in satellite sea-surface temperature by a rule of its own, on strength and
area [@noaa_blobtracker_2026]; that is the heatwave named above.

By that yardstick the well-known events are a few degrees. The regional mean on the peak day of the ten examples
@hobday2018 tabulate runs from 1.92 to 5.10 °C against 1983–2012; the largest is the Santa Barbara Channel in
October 2015, and the Northeast Pacific "Blob" is 2.56 °C. Eight prominent events reviewed by @smale2019 had maximum
intensities of "3.5 to 9.5°C above climatological SST". The `r fs(k$l50)` °C mean of the upper 50 m over
`r k$l50_n` stations is at the top of the first range, and it is a 50 m layer, not a skin temperature.

Below the surface the numbers are larger, and the literature says why: "These subsurface anomalies are often larger
than surface anomalies, due to the movement of the strong vertical temperature gradients around the thermocline"
[@capotondi2024]. At moorings in the tropical western Pacific the mean intensity of subsurface heatwaves "shows a
peak of about 5.2 °C at 150 m, and the maximal mean intensity reaches 8.9 °C" [@hu2021], and a model study finds
that deep-reaching events "tend to reach deepest along the west coasts of the Americas, especially in the California
Current System" [@kohn2024]. No published temperature departure found in the search behind this page, for California
or anywhere else, reaches `r f1(k$top_anom)` °C. That is weak evidence by itself, because papers report averages far
more often than single stations. The evidence for the record is the ranking above.

### How El Niño warms these waters {#sec-mechanism}

The review by @jacox2017clivar names three routes. The measurements on this page bear on two of them.

- **Waves along the coast.** "During an El Niño, these waves tend to deepen the pycnocline and nutricline"
  [@jacox2017clivar]: coastally trapped waves that travel poleward from the equator. Earlier events deepened the
  thermocline off Southern California by tens of metres in cruise and winter means: the mixed layer by 10 to 30 m
  in January 1958 [@reid1960], the 14 °C isotherm off San Diego by more than 40 m in winter 1982–83, and the
  thermocline along the coast "by 50 to 100 m" [@mclain1985]. At the record station in fall 2026 the density
  surfaces lay `r round(iso$dz[1])` to `r round(iso$dz[2])` m below their November depths ([above](#sec-isopycnals)).
- **Water from the south.** "anomalous advection of surface waters from the south, as observed during the 1997-98
  El Niño", which "may amplify surface warming and water column stratification" [@jacox2017clivar]. Its mark is
  salt, and [fall 2026 is the saltiest cruise on record in the inner Bight](#sec-salt).
- **Winds.** A changed atmosphere over the North Pacific weakens the winds that drive upwelling. A cruise does not
  measure this.

El Niños differ, and the same literature says so. The subsurface water of 1982–83 was fresher than normal, not
saltier [@simpson1984a]. Gliders in the 2009–10 event found isopycnals "abnormally deep" but "no anomalous water
masses in the region" [@todd2011]. In 2015–16 the effects on the California Current were "weaker than expected based
on tropical sea surface temperature anomalies" [@jacox2016]. And the background has moved: "An overall warming trend
of 1.3°C in the ocean surface, a deepening in the depth of the mean thermocline (18 m)" between 1950 and 1999
[@dilorenzo2005], which a fixed 1993–2013 normal folds into any recent departure.

## What this does and does not show {#sec-caveats}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coverage
d_cov <- q("
  SELECT CASE dataset_key WHEN 'calcofi_bottle' THEN 'bottle' ELSE 'CTD' END AS series, CAST((cruise_year // 10) * 10 AS INTEGER) || 's' AS decade,
         count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE anom IS NOT NULL) AS with_monthly_normal,
         count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE anom_season IS NOT NULL) AS with_seasonal_normal,
         CAST(round(100.0 * count(anom) / count(*)) AS INTEGER) AS pct_values_with_monthly_normal
  FROM cell GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY series DESC, decade")
n_site <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT site_key) AS n, min(line) AS l0, max(line) AS l1 FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL")
months <- q("SELECT DISTINCT cruise_month AS m FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1")$m
kable(d_cov, col.names = c("series", "decade", "cruises", "with a monthly normal", "with a seasonal normal", "% of values with a monthly normal"),
      caption = "How much of the record has a normal to compare with.")
```

```{r}
#| label: chk-ctd-full
#| include: false
# the one-metre table is read for seven cruises: every cast `sample` lists for them must be in the published objects
d_full <- q("
  WITH f AS (SELECT cruise_key, sample_key FROM obs_ctd_full UNION ALL SELECT cruise_key, sample_key FROM obs_ctd_full_base),
  a AS (SELECT cruise_key, count(DISTINCT sample_key) AS casts_1m FROM f GROUP BY cruise_key),
  s AS (SELECT cruise_key, count(*) AS casts FROM sample WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND sample_type = 'cast' GROUP BY cruise_key)
  SELECT a.cruise_key, CAST(substr(a.cruise_key, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year, a.casts_1m, s.casts FROM a JOIN s USING (cruise_key) ORDER BY 1")
ctd_full <- list(n_twice = sum(table(cc_release_sources(CAT, "obs_ctd_full")$urls) > 1))
stopifnot(nrow(d_full) == 7, d_full$casts_1m == d_full$casts)
```

- **"The record" is the part of the record with a baseline.** A normal exists for `r n_site$n` stations of the
  present grid (lines `r n_site$l0` to `r n_site$l1`) and for the months with at least five cruises in 1993–2013:
  `r paste(month.name[months], collapse = ", ")`. Earlier decades sampled other months and other stations far more
  often. "The largest on record" means the largest among `r d_share$n_cruises` of `r n_cruises_all` cruises.
  The baseline-free comparisons ([shared stations](#tbl-paired), [record temperatures](#fig-warmest)) and the
  [yardstick that reaches every station](#sec-whole-record) do not have this limit and give the same answer.
- **The baseline is thin.** `r n_base[1]` to `r n_base[2]` November cruises per bin on line 93.3. The
  [baseline table](#tbl-baseline) bounds what that can change: the peak departure stays between
  `r f1(base_rng[1])` and `r f1(base_rng[2])` °C.
- **Coverage.** `r n_st` stations in `r as.integer(cr$date_max - cr$date_min) + 1` days, where a full cruise
  occupies 65 to 75. The layer averages are over those stations only; a whole-grid average would be lower and
  cannot be computed for this cruise.
- **Preliminary.** The casts are one-metre averages processed at sea. Two sensors agreeing within
  `r f1(chk$pair_core$max, 3)` °C and bottle salinities agreeing within `r f1(btl$ds, 3)` leave little for final
  calibration to change.
- **Single values or layer averages.** A ranking of single values rewards the thermocline, where a displaced layer
  makes the largest numbers, and it is where bad values in old data surface. The layer average over fixed stations
  is the fairer claim. Both rank fall 2026 first.
- **Peaks between cruises.** CalCOFI samples four times a year. The peak of the 1997–98 El Niño on line 90 was caught
  because extra cruises were added that winter [@lynn1998], and one of them is not in the release
  ([above](#sec-literature)). An earlier event's largest departure may have fallen between cruises; so may this one's.
- **A defect in the published one-metre table does not reach this page.** In releases v2026.11.05 and v2026.11.09
  the supplemental table `obs_ctd_full` is published with most casts missing for 22 cruises between April 2015 and
  April 2026: a fault in the release export, found by the release's maintainers while this page was being written
  and now being corrected, not a fault in the data. Its trace is in the catalog, which lists `r ctd_full$n_twice` of that table's
  objects more than once. Every departure, ranking and layer mean on this page is computed from the thinned series
  (`obs_env`) and the `climatology` table, which are complete. The one-metre table is read for seven cruises only,
  fall 2026 and the six November cruises of the baseline (`r paste(sort(d_full$year[d_full$cruise_key != CRUISE]), collapse = ", ")`),
  and for each of them the published object holds every cast the release's `sample` table lists
  (`r fk(sum(d_full$casts))` casts in all, checked each time the page is rendered).
- **Cause.** These measurements describe the water. They do not attribute it, and [neither, yet, does NOAA](#sec-context):
  a marine heatwave has been in place off California since 2025 and a strong El Niño arrived on top of it.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

- **Data.** CalCOFI Integrated Database release `r VER`, read through its catalog with
  [`calcofi4r`](https://calcofi.io/calcofi4r/) (`cc_catalog()`, `cc_release_sources()`); every object is listed
  with its URL under [Data sources](#sec-data). Tables: `obs_env` (the thinned CTD series and the bottle series,
  with the release's quality predicate `qual_ok`), `climatology`, `obs_ctd_full` (one-metre CTD casts of the
  cruise), `sample`, `sample_measurement`, `cruise`.
- **A cell** is one cruise × station × 10 m depth bin of one series: the mean of its quality-ok values.
- **A departure** is a cell minus the `climatology` row of the same series, station, depth bin and measurement
  type for the cruise's month (`cruise.month_median`, the month of its median cast). The seasonal departure uses the
  row's `season_mean` (December–February, March–May, June–August, September–November).
- **A layer mean** averages a station's profile over every 10 m bin of the layer, after linear interpolation in
  depth between sampled bins (never across more than 60 m, never beyond the sampled range), and requires every bin.
  A cruise mean averages the stations.
- **The map's shading** is ordinary kriging by `calcofi4r::cc_interpolate()`, the interpolator of the Explorer's
  contour maps, clipped to the hull of the stations (plus 15 km), masked over land and limited to the range of the
  measured values. Colours are the cmocean maps [@thyng2016]. Density is TEOS-10 potential density anomaly, from the
  `gsw` package.
- **Mixed-layer depth** is the release's `mld_sigma_theta_0125`, in the registry's words
  "`r mt$description`" (`r mt$derivation`), with its own November normal. The release's headline criterion is
  stricter and stops at a thin warm skin on some casts; the looser one is used here because the question is how
  deep the warm layer reaches.
- **The whole-record yardstick** compares a cell with the mean of the other cruises, before fall 2026, of the same
  series at the same station, calendar month and depth bin, where at least five exist. Two casts that hold bad
  values ([shown above](#sec-rank)) are left out of it and of the per-event maxima.
- **Salinity across events** uses the bottle series' values and normals (bottle casts end in 2021), and the fall
  2026 CTD against the same bottle normals, because the CTD salinity normal carries unflagged spikes.
- **Published values** quoted under [context](#sec-context) were each read in the source cited, or in its abstract
  where the table says so; every quotation was checked against a saved copy of the text. Each entry of the
  bibliography was built from its Crossref or DataCite record.
- **Outside sources** (buoys, the Scripps Pier shore station, satellite analyses, Argo, the glider index) are fetched by
  `scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py` and kept as small tables in
  `data/2026-11_temperature-anomaly/`, because the buoy files hold only the last 45 days.

## Data sources {#sec-data}

Everything on this page is computed from public data. The release objects read, by the URL the release catalog
gives for each:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sources
d_src |>
  transmute(table, partition, `size (MB)` = round(mb, 1), url = glue("<a href='{url}'>{sub(paste0(BASE_URL, '/'), '', url, fixed = T)}</a>")) |>
  kable(escape = F, caption = glue("Objects of release {VER} read by this page ({f1(sum(d_src$mb), 0)} MB), under {BASE_URL}/."))
```

- Release catalog: <`r glue("{BASE_URL}/ducklake/releases/{VER}/catalog.json")`>
- Release citation: `r CAT$citation`
- The same section in the CalCOFI apps:
  [CTD transects](https://calcofi.io/ctd-transects/?line=93.3&cruise=2026-11-33P4&var=temperature_ave&mode=anomaly),
  the [Explorer's section](https://calcofi.io/explore/?lens=section&var=temperature&line=93.3&cruise=2026-11-33P4&anom=1)
  and its [3-D view](https://calcofi.io/explore/?lens=section&var=temperature&line=93.3&cruise=2026-11-33P4&anom=1&view=3d).

To cite this page: CalCOFI (2026). *The November 2026 temperature anomaly off Southern California.*
<https://calcofi.io/workflows/2026-11_temperature-anomaly.html>, with the release citation above for the data.

Outside sources, with the URL of every request and when it was made:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-outside-sources
d_osrc |>
  mutate(
    source = case_when(
      str_detect(url, "ndbc.noaa.gov")   ~ "NOAA National Data Buoy Center",
      str_detect(url, "Oisst")           ~ "NOAA OISST v2.1 (CoastWatch ERDDAP)",
      str_detect(url, "MUR")             ~ "JPL MUR SST v4.1 (CoastWatch ERDDAP)",
      str_detect(url, "ifremer")         ~ "Argo (Ifremer ERDDAP)",
      str_detect(url, "scripps-pier")    ~ "SCCOOS automated shore station, Scripps Pier (IOOS sensors ERDDAP)",
      str_detect(url, "spraydata")       ~ "Southern California Temperature Index, Scripps glider group (Spray ERDDAP)",
      TRUE                               ~ "other"),
    url = glue("<a href='{url}'>{str_trunc(url, 110)}</a>")) |>
  select(source, accessed_utc, status, url) |>
  dt_(escape = F, caption = "Every request to an outside source.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-buoy-stations
d_bstn |>
  transmute(
    buoy, name, latitude = lat, longitude = lon, `km to the nearest cast` = km_to_nearest_cast, `record read` = glue("{substr(first_utc, 1, 10)} to {substr(last_utc, 1, 10)}"),
    page = glue("<a href='{page}'>station page</a>"), data = glue("<a href='{url}'>realtime file</a>")) |>
  kable(escape = F, caption = "Buoys and the tide station read (NDBC keeps the last 45 days in these files).")
```

**The animation** is a page of its own in the Explorer's repository, driven by one clock and stepped frame by
frame into the video: [`story/elnino-2026/`](https://github.com/CalCOFI/explore/tree/9a20f0150798eb579987b29650c767604634a7c1/story/elnino-2026)
at the commit it was rendered from ([CalCOFI/explore#55](https://github.com/CalCOFI/explore/pull/55)).
`render.sh` is the whole pipeline in one command: it derives the page's data from the analysis database
(`build_data.sql`), builds the page, captures 900 frames in headless Chrome (`capture.mjs`) and encodes them with
`ffmpeg`. Its files, read from that commit:

```{r}
#| label: video-code
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# the animation's source, read from the explore repository at the commit the video was rendered from (cached)
EXPLORE_SHA <- "9a20f0150798eb579987b29650c767604634a7c1"
STORY_FILES <- c("README.md", "render.sh", "build_data.sh", "build_data.sql", "capture.mjs", "page/index.html", "page/main.ts", "page/terrain.ts", "page/style.css")
STORY_LANG  <- c(md = "markdown", sh = "bash", sql = "sql", mjs = "javascript", html = "html", ts = "typescript", css = "css")
for (f in STORY_FILES) {
  url  <- glue("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CalCOFI/explore/{EXPLORE_SHA}/story/elnino-2026/{f}")
  page <- glue("https://github.com/CalCOFI/explore/blob/{EXPLORE_SHA}/story/elnino-2026/{f}")
  path <- file.path(DIR_CACHE, "explore", EXPLORE_SHA, f)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = T, showWarnings = F)
    try(curl::curl_download(url, path, quiet = T), silent = T)}
  if (file.exists(path) && file.size(path) > 0) {
    src <- readLines(path, warn = F)
    cat(glue("<details><summary><a href='{page}'><code>story/elnino-2026/{f}</code></a> ({length(src)} lines)</summary>"), "\n\n", sep = "")
    cat("`````", STORY_LANG[[tools::file_ext(f)]], "\n", sep = ""); cat(src, sep = "\n"); cat("\n`````\n\n</details>\n\n")
  } else cat(glue("- [`story/elnino-2026/{f}`]({page})"), "\n\n", sep = "")}
```
